decl_147.name: FTC.Entry
decl_147.label: Entry
decl_147.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_147.source:
structure Entry (X : Type*) where
  point : X
  weight : ℝ
  weight_nonneg : 0 ≤ weight

/-- Weighted contribution of one separately indexed copy. -/

decl_653.name: FTC.contribution
decl_653.label: contribution
decl_653.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_653.statement: {I : Type u_1} → {S : Type u_2} → {X : Type u_3} → (X → S → ℝ) → (I → FTC.Entry X) → I → S → ℝ
decl_653.source:
def contribution (loss : X → S → ℝ) (entries : I → Entry X) (i : I) (s : S) : ℝ :=
  (entries i).weight * loss (entries i).point s

decl_656.name: FTC.contribution_nonneg
decl_656.label: contribution_nonneg
decl_656.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_656.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} {X : Type u_3} [DecidableEq I] (loss : X → S → ℝ) (entries : I → FTC.Entry X),
  (∀ (x : X) (s : S), 0 ≤ loss x s) → ∀ (i : I) (s : S), 0 ≤ FTC.contribution loss entries i s
decl_656.source:
theorem contribution_nonneg (loss : X → S → ℝ) (entries : I → Entry X)
    (h : ∀ x s, 0 ≤ loss x s) (i : I) (s : S) :
    0 ≤ contribution loss entries i s :=
  mul_nonneg (entries i).weight_nonneg (h _ _)

/-- Cost over the active indices, with inherited contributions. -/

decl_658.name: FTC.cost
decl_658.label: cost
decl_658.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_658.statement: {I : Type u_1} → {S : Type u_2} → (I → S → ℝ) → Finset I → S → ℝ

decl_541.name: FTC.IsCoreset
decl_541.label: IsCoreset
decl_541.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_541.statement: {S : Type u_2} → ℝ → (S → ℝ) → (S → ℝ) → Prop
decl_541.source:
def IsCoreset (ε : ℝ) (reference approx : S → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ s, (1 - ε) * reference s ≤ approx s ∧ approx s ≤ (1 + ε) * reference s

decl_665.name: FTC.cost_nonneg
decl_665.label: cost_nonneg
decl_665.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_665.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [DecidableEq I] {c : I → S → ℝ},
  (∀ (i : I) (s : S), 0 ≤ c i s) → ∀ (Q : Finset I) (s : S), 0 ≤ FTC.cost c Q s
decl_665.source:
theorem cost_nonneg {c : I → S → ℝ} (hc : ∀ i s, 0 ≤ c i s)
    (Q : Finset I) (s : S) : 0 ≤ cost c Q s :=
  Finset.sum_nonneg fun i _ => hc i s

decl_654.name: FTC.contribution_le_cost
decl_654.label: contribution_le_cost
decl_654.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_654.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [DecidableEq I] {c : I → S → ℝ},
  (∀ (i : I) (s : S), 0 ≤ c i s) → ∀ {Q : Finset I} {i : I}, i ∈ Q → ∀ (s : S), c i s ≤ FTC.cost c Q s
decl_654.source:
theorem contribution_le_cost {c : I → S → ℝ} (hc : ∀ i s, 0 ≤ c i s)
    {Q : Finset I} {i : I} (hi : i ∈ Q) (s : S) : c i s ≤ cost c Q s :=
  Finset.single_le_sum (fun j _ => hc j s) hi

decl_661.name: FTC.cost_eq_zero_contribution
decl_661.label: cost_eq_zero_contribution
decl_661.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_661.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [DecidableEq I] {c : I → S → ℝ},
  (∀ (i : I) (s : S), 0 ≤ c i s) → ∀ {Q : Finset I} {i : I}, i ∈ Q → ∀ {s : S}, FTC.cost c Q s = 0 → c i s = 0
decl_661.source:
theorem cost_eq_zero_contribution {c : I → S → ℝ} (hc : ∀ i s, 0 ≤ c i s)
    {Q : Finset I} {i : I} (hi : i ∈ Q) {s : S} (hzero : cost c Q s = 0) :
    c i s = 0 := by
  have hle := contribution_le_cost hc hi s
  rw [hzero] at hle
  exact le_antisymm hle (hc i s)

decl_664.name: FTC.cost_mono
decl_664.label: cost_mono
decl_664.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_664.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [DecidableEq I] {c : I → S → ℝ},
  (∀ (i : I) (s : S), 0 ≤ c i s) → ∀ {A B : Finset I}, A ⊆ B → ∀ (s : S), FTC.cost c A s ≤ FTC.cost c B s
decl_664.source:
theorem cost_mono {c : I → S → ℝ} (hc : ∀ i s, 0 ≤ c i s)
    {A B : Finset I} (h : A ⊆ B) (s : S) : cost c A s ≤ cost c B s :=
  Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg h (fun i _ _ => hc i s)

decl_659.name: FTC.cost_congr
decl_659.label: cost_congr
decl_659.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_659.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [DecidableEq I] {c d : I → S → ℝ} {Q : Finset I},
  (∀ i ∈ Q, ∀ (s : S), c i s = d i s) → ∀ (s : S), FTC.cost c Q s = FTC.cost d Q s

decl_660.name: FTC.cost_empty
decl_660.label: cost_empty
decl_660.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_660.statement: ∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [DecidableEq I] (c : I → S → ℝ) (s : S), FTC.cost c ∅ s = 0
decl_660.source:
@[simp] theorem cost_empty (c : I → S → ℝ) (s : S) : cost c ∅ s = 0 := by
  simp [cost]

decl_667.name: FTC.cost_sdiff_add_inter
decl_667.label: cost_sdiff_add_inter
decl_667.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_667.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq I] (c : I → S → ℝ) (Q B : Finset I) (s : S),
  FTC.cost c (Q \ B) s + FTC.cost c (Q ∩ B) s = FTC.cost c Q s
decl_667.source:
theorem cost_sdiff_add_inter (c : I → S → ℝ) (Q B : Finset I) (s : S) :
    cost c (Q \ B) s + cost c (Q ∩ B) s = cost c Q s := by
  unfold cost
  rw [← Finset.sum_union (Finset.disjoint_sdiff_inter Q B), Finset.sdiff_union_inter]

decl_666.name: FTC.cost_sdiff_add
decl_666.label: cost_sdiff_add
decl_666.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_666.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq I] (c : I → S → ℝ) {Q A : Finset I},
  A ⊆ Q → ∀ (s : S), FTC.cost c (Q \ A) s + FTC.cost c A s = FTC.cost c Q s
decl_666.source:
theorem cost_sdiff_add (c : I → S → ℝ) {Q A : Finset I} (h : A ⊆ Q) (s : S) :
    cost c (Q \ A) s + cost c A s = cost c Q s := by
  simpa [Finset.inter_eq_right.mpr h] using cost_sdiff_add_inter c Q A s

decl_663.name: FTC.cost_le_card_mul
decl_663.label: cost_le_card_mul
decl_663.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_663.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [DecidableEq I] {c : I → S → ℝ} {Q : Finset I} {b : ℝ} {s : S},
  (∀ i ∈ Q, c i s ≤ b) → FTC.cost c Q s ≤ ↑Q.card * b
decl_663.source:
theorem cost_le_card_mul {c : I → S → ℝ} {Q : Finset I} {b : ℝ} {s : S}
    (h : ∀ i ∈ Q, c i s ≤ b) : cost c Q s ≤ (Q.card : ℝ) * b := by
  calc
    cost c Q s ≤ ∑ _i ∈ Q, b := Finset.sum_le_sum h
    _ = (Q.card : ℝ) * b := by simp

decl_662.name: FTC.cost_erase_add
decl_662.label: cost_erase_add
decl_662.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Basic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_662.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq I] (c : I → S → ℝ) {Q : Finset I} {i : I},
  i ∈ Q → ∀ (s : S), FTC.cost c (Q.erase i) s + c i s = FTC.cost c Q s
decl_662.source:
theorem cost_erase_add (c : I → S → ℝ) {Q : Finset I} {i : I}
    (hi : i ∈ Q) (s : S) : cost c (Q.erase i) s + c i s = cost c Q s := by
  exact Finset.sum_erase_add _ _ hi

end FTC

decl_542.name: FTC.IsFCorruption
decl_542.label: IsFCorruption
decl_542.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Corruption.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_542.statement: {I : Type u_1} → {X : Type u_2} → ℕ → Finset I → (I → FTC.Entry X) → (I → FTC.Entry X) → Prop
decl_542.source:
def IsFCorruption (f : ℕ) (U : Finset I) (original corrupted : I → Entry X) : Prop :=
  ∃ B ⊆ U, B.card ≤ f ∧ ∀ i ∈ U, i ∉ B → corrupted i = original i

decl_543.name: FTC.IsFCorruption.refl
decl_543.label: IsFCorruption.refl
decl_543.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Corruption.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_543.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {X : Type u_2} [DecidableEq I] (f : ℕ) (U : Finset I) (entries : I → FTC.Entry X),
  FTC.IsFCorruption f U entries entries
decl_543.source:
theorem IsFCorruption.refl (f : ℕ) (U : Finset I) (entries : I → Entry X) :
    IsFCorruption f U entries entries := by
  exact ⟨∅, Finset.empty_subset _, by simp, by intros; rfl⟩

/-- Deterministic success event from Definition 2.1. The decoder observes only
the corrupted entries, returns active indices, and inherits their weights.
The probability of this event is handled separately in `Sampling.lean`. -/

decl_544.name: FTC.IsFilteringFaultTolerant
decl_544.label: IsFilteringFaultTolerant
decl_544.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Corruption.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_544.statement:
{I : Type u_1} →
  {X : Type u_2} →
    {S : Type u_3} →
      ℝ → ℕ → (S → ℝ) → (X → S → ℝ) → Finset I → (I → FTC.Entry X) → ((I → FTC.Entry X) → Finset I) → Prop
decl_544.source:
def IsFilteringFaultTolerant (ε : ℝ) (f : ℕ) (reference : S → ℝ)
    (loss : X → S → ℝ) (U : Finset I) (entries : I → Entry X)
    (decoder : (I → Entry X) → Finset I) : Prop :=
  IsCoreset ε reference (cost (contribution loss entries) U) ∧
    ∀ corrupted, IsFCorruption f U entries corrupted →
      decoder corrupted ⊆ U ∧
        IsCoreset ε reference (cost (contribution loss corrupted) (decoder corrupted))

end FTC

decl_101.name: FTC.Counterexample.proxyScore
decl_101.label: Counterexample.proxyScore
decl_101.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Example.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_101.statement: {n : ℕ} → (M : ℝ) → 1 ≤ M → Fin n → Fin n → FTC.Counterexample.Query n → Finset (Fin n) → Fin n → ℝ
decl_101.source:
noncomputable def proxyScore {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad first : Fin n) (A : Query n) : Finset (Fin n) → Fin n → ℝ :=
  fun _ i => proxy M hM bad first A i

decl_47.name: FTC.Counterexample.corruption_one
decl_47.label: Counterexample.corruption_one
decl_47.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Example.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_47.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (bad : Fin n),
  FTC.IsFCorruption 1 Finset.univ FTC.Counterexample.cleanEntries (FTC.Counterexample.corruptedEntries bad)
decl_47.source:
theorem corruption_one {n : ℕ} (bad : Fin n) :
    FTC.IsFCorruption 1 Finset.univ cleanEntries (corruptedEntries bad) := by
  refine ⟨{bad}, by simp, by simp, ?_⟩
  intro i _ hi
  have hib : i ≠ bad := by simpa using hi
  simp [corruptedEntries, cleanEntries, hib]

decl_24.name: FTC.Counterexample.clean_is_exact
decl_24.label: Counterexample.clean_is_exact
decl_24.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Example.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_24.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  FTC.IsCoreset 0 (FTC.Counterexample.cleanCost M hM) (FTC.cost (FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution M hM) Finset.univ)
decl_24.source:
theorem clean_is_exact {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) :
    FTC.IsCoreset 0 (cleanCost (n := n) M hM)
      (FTC.cost (cleanContribution M hM) Finset.univ) := by
  intro S
  simp [cleanCost]

decl_109.name: FTC.Counterexample.proxy_peel_output
decl_109.label: Counterexample.proxy_peel_output
decl_109.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Example.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_109.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  8 ≤ n →
    M ^ 2 = ↑n - 4 →
      ∀ (bad first j : Fin n),
        ↑first = 0 →
          ↑j ≠ 0 →
            ↑bad ≠ 0 →
              bad ≠ j →
                FTC.peel (FTC.Counterexample.proxyScore M hM bad first (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j)) 1
                    Finset.univ =
                  Finset.univ.erase first
decl_109.source:
theorem proxy_peel_output {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 8 ≤ n) (hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4) (bad first j : Fin n)
    (hfirst : first.val = 0) (hj : j.val ≠ 0) (hbad : bad.val ≠ 0) (hbj : bad ≠ j) :
    FTC.peel (proxyScore M hM bad first (referenceQuery j)) 1 Finset.univ =
      Finset.univ.erase first := by
  apply peel_one_of_strict_max _ _ first (Finset.mem_univ first)
  intro i _ hi
  exact proxy_strict_max M hM hn hM2 bad first j i hfirst hj hbad hbj hi

decl_54.name: FTC.Counterexample.exact_peel_output
decl_54.label: Counterexample.exact_peel_output
decl_54.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Example.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_54.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  8 ≤ n →
    M ^ 2 = ↑n - 4 →
      ∀ (bad j l : Fin n),
        j ≠ l →
          bad ≠ j →
            bad ≠ l →
              FTC.peel (FTC.sensitivity (FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad)) 1 Finset.univ =
                Finset.univ.erase bad
decl_54.source:
theorem exact_peel_output {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 8 ≤ n) (hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4)
    (bad j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l) (hbj : bad ≠ j) (hbl : bad ≠ l) :
    FTC.peel (FTC.sensitivity (corruptContribution M hM bad)) 1 Finset.univ =
      Finset.univ.erase bad := by
  apply peel_one_of_strict_max _ _ bad (Finset.mem_univ bad)
  intro i _ hi
  exact corruption_strict_sensitivity_max M hM hn hM2 bad j l hjl hbj hbl i hi

/-- Exact distortion at the explicit query `{p_j,p_l}` after proxy deletion. -/

decl_107.name: FTC.Counterexample.proxy_output_distortion
decl_107.label: Counterexample.proxy_output_distortion
decl_107.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Example.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_107.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  M ^ 2 = ↑n - 4 →
    ∀ (bad first j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l),
      bad ≠ j →
        bad ≠ l →
          first ≠ bad →
            first ≠ j →
              first ≠ l →
                FTC.cost (FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad) (Finset.univ.erase first)
                      (FTC.Counterexample.simplexQuery j l hjl) /
                    FTC.Counterexample.cleanCost M hM (FTC.Counterexample.simplexQuery j l hjl) =
                  FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.wrongDistortion ↑n
decl_107.source:
theorem proxy_output_distortion {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4) (bad first j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l)
    (hbj : bad ≠ j) (hbl : bad ≠ l) (hfb : first ≠ bad)
    (hfj : first ≠ j) (hfl : first ≠ l) :
    FTC.cost (corruptContribution M hM bad) (Finset.univ.erase first)
        (simplexQuery j l hjl) / cleanCost M hM (simplexQuery j l hjl) =
      wrongDistortion (n : ℝ) := by
  rw [cost_erase_first_simplex M hM bad first j l hjl hbj hbl hfb hfj hfl,
    cleanCost_simplex, hM2]
  unfold wrongDistortion
  congr 1
  ring

decl_108.name: FTC.Counterexample.proxy_output_not_coreset
decl_108.label: Counterexample.proxy_output_not_coreset
decl_108.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Example.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_108.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (ε : ℝ),
  0 < ε →
    ε < 1 / 10 →
      8 / ε ≤ ↑n →
        M ^ 2 = ↑n - 4 →
          ∀ (bad first j l : Fin n),
            j ≠ l →
              bad ≠ j →
                bad ≠ l →
                  first ≠ bad →
                    first ≠ j →
                      first ≠ l →
                        ¬FTC.IsCoreset (6 * ε) (FTC.Counterexample.cleanCost M hM)
                            (FTC.cost (FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad) (Finset.univ.erase first))
decl_108.source:
theorem proxy_output_not_coreset {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (hεsmall : ε < 1 / 10) (hn : 8 / ε ≤ (n : ℝ))
    (hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4) (bad first j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l)
    (hbj : bad ≠ j) (hbl : bad ≠ l) (hfb : first ≠ bad)
    (hfj : first ≠ j) (hfl : first ≠ l) :
    ¬ FTC.IsCoreset (6 * ε) (cleanCost M hM)
      (FTC.cost (corruptContribution M hM bad) (Finset.univ.erase first)) := by
  intro hco
  have hn8 := size_ge_eight hε hεsmall hn
  have hcpos : 0 < cleanCost M hM (simplexQuery j l hjl) := by
    rw [cleanCost_simplex]
    linarith
  have hratio := proxy_output_distortion M hM hM2 bad first j l hjl hbj hbl hfb hfj hfl
  have hgt := wrongDistortion_gt_tolerance hε hεsmall hn
  rw [← hratio] at hgt
  have hcostgt := (lt_div_iff₀ hcpos).mp hgt
  exact (not_le_of_gt hcostgt) (hco (simplexQuery j l hjl)).2

/-- All claims of the unnumbered Appendix A.1 counterexample, for one size.
The carrier is the actual finite metric `Vertex n` with `metricSpace M one_le_M`;
all costs and both decoders below operate on its actual two-center queries. -/

decl_3.name: FTC.Counterexample.ProxyFailureAtSize
decl_3.label: Counterexample.ProxyFailureAtSize
decl_3.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Example.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_3.source:
structure ProxyFailureAtSize (n : ℕ) (ε : ℝ) where
  M : ℝ
  one_le_M : 1 ≤ M
  M_sq : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4
  bad : Fin n
  first : Fin n
  j : Fin n
  first_zero : first.val = 0
  j_nonzero : j.val ≠ 0
  bad_nonzero : bad.val ≠ 0
  singleton_genuine : first ≠ bad
  initial_exact : FTC.IsCoreset 0 (cleanCost (n := n) M one_le_M)
    (FTC.cost (cleanContribution M one_le_M) Finset.univ)
  admissible_corruption : FTC.IsFCorruption 1 Finset.univ cleanEntries (corruptedEntries bad)
  clean_sensitivity : ∀ i : Fin n,
    FTC.sensitivity (cleanContribution M one_le_M) Finset.univ i = 1 / ((n : ℝ) - 2)
  good_sensitivity : ∀ i : Fin n, i ≠ bad →
    FTC.sensitivity (corruptContribution M one_le_M bad) Finset.univ i ≤ 1 / ((n : ℝ) - 3)
  reference_cost : corruptCost M one_le_M bad (referenceQuery j) = referenceCost (n : ℝ)
  reference_two_approx : ∀ S : Query n,
    corruptCost M one_le_M bad (referenceQuery j) ≤ 2 * corruptCost M one_le_M bad S
  reference_nearest : ∀ i : Fin n,
    if i = first then graphDist M (corruptedEntries bad i).point a <
      graphDist M (corruptedEntries bad i).point (p j)
    else graphDist M (corruptedEntries bad i).point (p j) <
      graphDist M (corruptedEntries bad i).point a
  proxy_valid : ∀ i : Fin n,
    FTC.sensitivity (corruptContribution M one_le_M bad) Finset.univ i ≤
      proxy M one_le_M bad first (referenceQuery j) i
  proxy_unique_max : ∀ i : Fin n, i ≠ first →
    proxy M one_le_M bad first (referenceQuery j) i <
      proxy M one_le_M bad first (referenceQuery j) first
  exact_unique_max : ∀ i : Fin n, i ≠ bad →
    FTC.sensitivity (corruptContribution M one_le_M bad) Finset.univ i <
      FTC.sensitivity (corruptContribution M one_le_M bad) Finset.univ bad
  proxy_output : FTC.peel (proxyScore M one_le_M bad first (referenceQuery j)) 1 Finset.univ =
    Finset.univ.erase first
  exact_output : FTC.peel (FTC.sensitivity (corruptContribution M one_le_M bad)) 1 Finset.univ =
    Finset.univ.erase bad
  proxy_distortion : ∃ S : Query n,
    FTC.cost (corruptContribution M one_le_M bad) (Finset.univ.erase first) S /
      cleanCost M one_le_M S = wrongDistortion (n : ℝ)
  proxy_fails : ¬ FTC.IsCoreset (6 * ε) (cleanCost M one_le_M)
    (FTC.cost (corruptContribution M one_le_M bad)
      (FTC.peel (proxyScore M one_le_M bad first (referenceQuery j)) 1 Finset.univ))
  exact_succeeds : FTC.IsCoreset ε (cleanCost M one_le_M)
    (FTC.cost (corruptContribution M one_le_M bad)
      (FTC.peel (FTC.sensitivity (corruptContribution M one_le_M bad)) 1 Finset.univ))

/-- Full counterexample for every parameter choice in the source PDF.
`M = sqrt(n-4)`, `first = 0`, reference center `j = 1`, witness's other center
`l = 2`, and the corrupted index `bad = n-1` discharge all construction
hypotheses. There are no assumed metric, sensitivity, or decoder claims. -/

decl_7.name: FTC.Counterexample.appendix_A1_counterexample
decl_7.label: Appendix A.1 · Metric counterexample
decl_7.summary: Constructs the Appendix A.1 metric counterexample and establishes the decoder separation.
decl_7.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} {ε : ℝ}, 0 < ε → ε < 1 / 10 → 8 / ε ≤ ↑n → Nonempty (FTC.Counterexample.ProxyFailureAtSize n ε)
decl_7.source:
theorem appendix_A1_counterexample {n : ℕ} {ε : ℝ}
    (hε : 0 < ε) (hεsmall : ε < 1 / 10) (hn : 8 / ε ≤ (n : ℝ)) :
    Nonempty (ProxyFailureAtSize n ε) := by
  have hnR : (8 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := size_ge_eight hε hεsmall hn
  have hn8 : 8 ≤ n := by exact_mod_cast hnR
  let M : ℝ := Real.sqrt ((n : ℝ) - 4)
  have hM0 : 0 ≤ M := Real.sqrt_nonneg _
  have hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4 := Real.sq_sqrt (by linarith)
  have hM : 1 ≤ M := by nlinarith
  let first : Fin n := ⟨0, by omega⟩
  let j : Fin n := ⟨1, by omega⟩
  let l : Fin n := ⟨2, by omega⟩
  let bad : Fin n := ⟨n - 1, by omega⟩
  have hf : first.val = 0 := rfl
  have hj : j.val ≠ 0 := by norm_num [j]
  have hb : bad.val ≠ 0 := by dsimp [bad]; omega
  have hjl : j ≠ l := by intro h; have := congrArg Fin.val h; norm_num [j, l] at this
  have hbj : bad ≠ j := by intro h; have := congrArg Fin.val h; dsimp [bad, j] at this; omega
  have hbl : bad ≠ l := by intro h; have := congrArg Fin.val h; dsimp [bad, l] at this; omega
  have hfb : first ≠ bad := by intro h; have := congrArg Fin.val h; dsimp [first, bad] at this; omega
  have hfj : first ≠ j := by intro h; have := congrArg Fin.val h; norm_num [first, j] at this
  have hfl : first ≠ l := by intro h; have := congrArg Fin.val h; norm_num [first, l] at this
  have hpout := proxy_peel_output M hM hn8 hM2 bad first j hf hj hb hbj
  have heout := exact_peel_output M hM hn8 hM2 bad j l hjl hbj hbl
  refine ⟨{
    M := M, one_le_M := hM, M_sq := hM2,
    bad := bad, first := first, j := j,
    first_zero := hf, j_nonzero := hj, bad_nonzero := hb, singleton_genuine := hfb,
    initial_exact := clean_is_exact M hM,
    admissible_corruption := corruption_one bad,
    clean_sensitivity := clean_sensitivity_eq M hM (by omega),
    good_sensitivity := fun i hi => corrupt_good_sensitivity_le M hM (by omega) bad i hi,
    reference_cost := reference_cost_formula M hM hM2 bad first j hf hj hb hbj,
    reference_two_approx := reference_is_two_approx M hM hn8 hM2 bad first j hf hj hb hbj,
    reference_nearest := reference_assignment_nearest M bad first j hf hj hb,
    proxy_valid := fun i => sensitivity_le_proxy M hM hn8 hM2 bad first j i hf hj hb hbj,
    proxy_unique_max := fun i hi => proxy_strict_max M hM hn8 hM2 bad first j i hf hj hb hbj hi,
    exact_unique_max := fun i hi => corruption_strict_sensitivity_max M hM hn8 hM2 bad j l hjl hbj hbl i hi,
    proxy_output := hpout, exact_output := heout,
    proxy_distortion := ⟨simplexQuery j l hjl,
      proxy_output_distortion M hM hM2 bad first j l hjl hbj hbl hfb hfj hfl⟩,
    proxy_fails := ?_, exact_succeeds := ?_ }⟩
  · rw [hpout]
    exact proxy_output_not_coreset M hM ε hε hεsmall hn hM2 bad first j l hjl hbj hbl hfb hfj hfl
  · rw [heout]
    exact exact_deletion_isCoreset M hM (by omega) bad ε hε.le
      (distortion_and_deletion_bounds hε hεsmall hn).2.2

end FTC.Counterexample

decl_122.name: FTC.Counterexample.sum_lower_bound_of_flat
decl_122.label: Counterexample.sum_lower_bound_of_flat
decl_122.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatBounds.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_122.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq I] (Q E : Finset I) (c : I → ℝ) (L : ℝ),
  (∀ (i : I), 0 ≤ c i) → 0 ≤ L → (∀ i ∈ Q \ E, c i = L) → (↑Q.card - ↑E.card) * L ≤ ∑ i ∈ Q, c i
decl_122.source:
theorem sum_lower_bound_of_flat
    (Q E : Finset I) (c : I → ℝ) (L : ℝ)
    (hc : ∀ i, 0 ≤ c i) (hL : 0 ≤ L)
    (hflat : ∀ i ∈ Q \ E, c i = L) :
    ((Q.card : ℝ) - (E.card : ℝ)) * L ≤ ∑ i ∈ Q, c i := by
  have hcard : (Q.card : ℝ) - (E.card : ℝ) ≤ ((Q \ E).card : ℝ) := by
    have h := Finset.card_le_card_sdiff_add_card (s := Q) (t := E)
    have hr : (Q.card : ℝ) ≤ ((Q \ E).card : ℝ) + (E.card : ℝ) := by
      exact_mod_cast h
    linarith
  calc
    ((Q.card : ℝ) - (E.card : ℝ)) * L ≤ ((Q \ E).card : ℝ) * L :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hcard hL
    _ = ∑ i ∈ Q \ E, c i := by
      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl hflat]
      simp
    _ ≤ ∑ i ∈ Q, c i :=
      Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg Finset.sdiff_subset (fun i _ _ => hc i)

/-- At most two exceptions give a uniform contribution bound for every
entry below the common level. The total may include additional bad entries. -/

decl_34.name: FTC.Counterexample.contribution_mul_card_sub_two_le
decl_34.label: Counterexample.contribution_mul_card_sub_two_le
decl_34.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatBounds.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_34.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq I] (Q E : Finset I) (c : I → ℝ) (L : ℝ),
  (∀ (i : I), 0 ≤ c i) →
    0 ≤ L → (∀ i ∈ Q \ E, c i = L) → E.card ≤ 2 → 2 ≤ Q.card → ∀ {i : I}, c i ≤ L → (↑Q.card - 2) * c i ≤ ∑ j ∈ Q, c j
decl_34.source:
theorem contribution_mul_card_sub_two_le
    (Q E : Finset I) (c : I → ℝ) (L : ℝ)
    (hc : ∀ i, 0 ≤ c i) (hL : 0 ≤ L)
    (hflat : ∀ i ∈ Q \ E, c i = L) (hE : E.card ≤ 2)
    (hQ : 2 ≤ Q.card) {i : I} (hi : c i ≤ L) :
    ((Q.card : ℝ) - 2) * c i ≤ ∑ j ∈ Q, c j := by
  have hq : 0 ≤ (Q.card : ℝ) - 2 := by
    have h : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (Q.card : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hQ
    linarith
  have he : (E.card : ℝ) ≤ 2 := by exact_mod_cast hE
  calc
    ((Q.card : ℝ) - 2) * c i ≤ ((Q.card : ℝ) - 2) * L :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hi hq
    _ ≤ ((Q.card : ℝ) - (E.card : ℝ)) * L :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (by linarith) hL
    _ ≤ ∑ j ∈ Q, c j := sum_lower_bound_of_flat Q E c L hc hL hflat

/-- At most two entries can receive an exceptional label from two centers. -/

decl_12.name: FTC.Counterexample.card_biUnion_le_two
decl_12.label: Counterexample.card_biUnion_le_two
decl_12.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatBounds.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_12.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq I] {X : Type u_2} [DecidableEq X] (C : Finset X) (exceptional : X → Finset I),
  C.card = 2 → (∀ (x : X), (exceptional x).card ≤ 1) → (C.biUnion exceptional).card ≤ 2
decl_12.source:
theorem card_biUnion_le_two {X : Type*} [DecidableEq X]
    (C : Finset X) (exceptional : X → Finset I)
    (hC : C.card = 2) (hex : ∀ x, (exceptional x).card ≤ 1) :
    (C.biUnion exceptional).card ≤ 2 := by
  calc
    (C.biUnion exceptional).card ≤ ∑ x ∈ C, (exceptional x).card :=
      Finset.card_biUnion_le
    _ ≤ ∑ _x ∈ C, 1 := Finset.sum_le_sum (fun x _ => hex x)
    _ = 2 := by simp [hC]

end FTC.Counterexample

decl_31.name: FTC.Counterexample.commonLevel
decl_31.label: Counterexample.commonLevel
decl_31.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_31.source:
noncomputable def commonLevel {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (S : Query n) : ℝ :=
  S.centers.inf' S.nonempty (fun v => baseline M v ^ 2)

/-- Union of the at-most-one original-point exceptions of the two centers. -/

decl_111.name: FTC.Counterexample.queryExceptions
decl_111.label: Counterexample.queryExceptions
decl_111.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_111.source:
def queryExceptions {n : ℕ} (S : Query n) : Finset (Fin n) :=
  S.centers.biUnion exceptional

decl_112.name: FTC.Counterexample.queryExceptions_card_le_two
decl_112.label: Counterexample.queryExceptions_card_le_two
decl_112.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_112.source:
theorem queryExceptions_card_le_two {n : ℕ} (S : Query n) :
    (queryExceptions S).card ≤ 2 :=
  card_biUnion_le_two S.centers exceptional S.card_eq exceptional_card_le_one

decl_82.name: FTC.Counterexample.one_le_commonLevel
decl_82.label: Counterexample.one_le_commonLevel
decl_82.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_82.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ), 1 ≤ M → ∀ (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n), 1 ≤ FTC.Counterexample.commonLevel M S
decl_82.source:
theorem one_le_commonLevel {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (S : Query n) :
    1 ≤ commonLevel M S := by
  apply Finset.le_inf'
  intro v _
  have hv := one_le_baseline M hM v
  nlinarith

decl_33.name: FTC.Counterexample.commonLevel_nonneg
decl_33.label: Counterexample.commonLevel_nonneg
decl_33.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_33.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ), 1 ≤ M → ∀ (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n), 0 ≤ FTC.Counterexample.commonLevel M S
decl_33.source:
theorem commonLevel_nonneg {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (S : Query n) :
    0 ≤ commonLevel M S := le_trans (by norm_num) (one_le_commonLevel M hM S)

decl_93.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_le_commonLevel
decl_93.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_le_commonLevel
decl_93.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_93.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (i : Fin n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
  FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM (FTC.Counterexample.p i) S ≤ FTC.Counterexample.commonLevel M S
decl_93.source:
theorem pointLoss_le_commonLevel {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (i : Fin n) (S : Query n) : pointLoss M hM (p i) S ≤ commonLevel M S := by
  apply Finset.le_inf'
  intro v hv
  have hpoint : pointLoss M hM (p i) S ≤ graphDist M (p i) v ^ 2 := by
    rw [pointLoss_eq_inf]
    exact Finset.inf'_le _ hv
  have hcap : graphDist M (p i) v ^ 2 ≤ baseline M v ^ 2 := by
    exact (sq_le_sq₀ (graphDist_nonneg M hM _ _) (baseline_nonneg M hM v)).2
      (graphDist_le_baseline M i v)
  exact hpoint.trans hcap

/-- Every original point outside at most two exceptions has the common loss. -/

decl_90.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_eq_commonLevel_of_notMem
decl_90.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_eq_commonLevel_of_notMem
decl_90.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_90.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (i : Fin n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
  i ∉ FTC.Counterexample.queryExceptions S →
    FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM (FTC.Counterexample.p i) S = FTC.Counterexample.commonLevel M S
decl_90.source:
theorem pointLoss_eq_commonLevel_of_notMem {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (i : Fin n) (S : Query n) (hi : i ∉ queryExceptions S) :
    pointLoss M hM (p i) S = commonLevel M S := by
  apply le_antisymm (pointLoss_le_commonLevel M hM i S)
  rw [pointLoss_eq_inf]
  apply Finset.le_inf'
  intro v hv
  have hinot : i ∉ exceptional v := by
    intro h
    exact hi (Finset.mem_biUnion.mpr ⟨v, hv, h⟩)
  rw [graphDist_eq_baseline_of_notMem M i v hinot]
  exact Finset.inf'_le _ hv

decl_32.name: FTC.Counterexample.commonLevel_mul_card_sub_two_le_cost
decl_32.label: Counterexample.commonLevel_mul_card_sub_two_le_cost
decl_32.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_32.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (G : Finset (Fin n)) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
  (↑G.card - 2) * FTC.Counterexample.commonLevel M S ≤ FTC.cost (FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution M hM) G S
decl_32.source:
theorem commonLevel_mul_card_sub_two_le_cost {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (G : Finset (Fin n)) (S : Query n) :
    ((G.card : ℝ) - 2) * commonLevel M S ≤ FTC.cost (cleanContribution M hM) G S := by
  have he : ((queryExceptions S).card : ℝ) ≤ 2 := by
    exact_mod_cast queryExceptions_card_le_two S
  calc
    ((G.card : ℝ) - 2) * commonLevel M S ≤
        ((G.card : ℝ) - ((queryExceptions S).card : ℝ)) * commonLevel M S :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (by linarith) (commonLevel_nonneg M hM S)
    _ ≤ ∑ i ∈ G, cleanContribution M hM i S := by
      apply sum_lower_bound_of_flat G (queryExceptions S)
        (fun i => cleanContribution M hM i S) (commonLevel M S)
        (fun i => cleanContribution_nonneg M hM i S) (commonLevel_nonneg M hM S)
      intro i hi
      simp only [cleanContribution_apply]
      exact pointLoss_eq_commonLevel_of_notMem M hM i S (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hi).2
    _ = FTC.cost (cleanContribution M hM) G S := rfl

decl_94.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_mul_card_sub_two_le_cost
decl_94.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_mul_card_sub_two_le_cost
decl_94.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_94.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (G : Finset (Fin n)),
  2 ≤ G.card →
    ∀ (i : Fin n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
      (↑G.card - 2) * FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM (FTC.Counterexample.p i) S ≤
        FTC.cost (FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution M hM) G S
decl_94.source:
theorem pointLoss_mul_card_sub_two_le_cost {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (G : Finset (Fin n)) (hG : 2 ≤ G.card) (i : Fin n) (S : Query n) :
    ((G.card : ℝ) - 2) * pointLoss M hM (p i) S ≤
      FTC.cost (cleanContribution M hM) G S := by
  have hcoef : 0 ≤ (G.card : ℝ) - 2 := by
    have h : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (G.card : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hG
    linarith
  exact (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (pointLoss_le_commonLevel M hM i S) hcoef).trans
    (commonLevel_mul_card_sub_two_le_cost M hM G S)

decl_15.name: FTC.Counterexample.card_sub_two_le_cost
decl_15.label: Counterexample.card_sub_two_le_cost
decl_15.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_15.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (G : Finset (Fin n)),
  2 ≤ G.card →
    ∀ (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n), ↑G.card - 2 ≤ FTC.cost (FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution M hM) G S
decl_15.source:
theorem card_sub_two_le_cost {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (G : Finset (Fin n)) (hG : 2 ≤ G.card) (S : Query n) :
    (G.card : ℝ) - 2 ≤ FTC.cost (cleanContribution M hM) G S := by
  have hcoef : 0 ≤ (G.card : ℝ) - 2 := by
    have h : (2 : ℝ) ≤ (G.card : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hG
    linarith
  calc
    (G.card : ℝ) - 2 = ((G.card : ℝ) - 2) * 1 := by ring
    _ ≤ ((G.card : ℝ) - 2) * commonLevel M S :=
      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (one_le_commonLevel M hM S) hcoef
    _ ≤ FTC.cost (cleanContribution M hM) G S :=
      commonLevel_mul_card_sub_two_le_cost M hM G S

decl_51.name: FTC.Counterexample.cost_good_eq_clean
decl_51.label: Counterexample.cost_good_eq_clean
decl_51.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_51.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (bad : Fin n) (G : Finset (Fin n)),
  bad ∉ G →
    ∀ (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
      FTC.cost (FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad) G S =
        FTC.cost (FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution M hM) G S
decl_51.source:
theorem cost_good_eq_clean {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad : Fin n) (G : Finset (Fin n)) (hG : bad ∉ G) (S : Query n) :
    FTC.cost (corruptContribution M hM bad) G S = FTC.cost (cleanContribution M hM) G S := by
  apply FTC.cost_congr
  intro i hi T
  have hib : i ≠ bad := by intro h; subst i; exact hG hi
  simp [corruptContribution_apply, hib]

decl_27.name: FTC.Counterexample.clean_uniform_bound
decl_27.label: Counterexample.clean_uniform_bound
decl_27.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_27.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  2 ≤ n →
    ∀ (i : Fin n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
      (↑n - 2) * FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution M hM i S ≤ FTC.Counterexample.cleanCost M hM S
decl_27.source:
theorem clean_uniform_bound {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 2 ≤ n) (i : Fin n) (S : Query n) :
    ((n : ℝ) - 2) * cleanContribution M hM i S ≤ cleanCost M hM S := by
  simpa [cleanCost] using pointLoss_mul_card_sub_two_le_cost M hM
    (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)) (by simpa) i S

decl_45.name: FTC.Counterexample.corrupt_uniform_good_bound
decl_45.label: Counterexample.corrupt_uniform_good_bound
decl_45.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_45.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  3 ≤ n →
    ∀ (bad i : Fin n),
      i ≠ bad →
        ∀ (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
          (↑n - 3) * FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad i S ≤ FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost M hM bad S
decl_45.source:
theorem corrupt_uniform_good_bound {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 3 ≤ n) (bad i : Fin n) (hib : i ≠ bad) (S : Query n) :
    ((n : ℝ) - 3) * corruptContribution M hM bad i S ≤ corruptCost M hM bad S := by
  let G := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).erase bad
  have hcard := Finset.card_erase_add_one (Finset.mem_univ bad)
  have hcardR : (G.card : ℝ) + 1 = (n : ℝ) := by
    have hcN : G.card + 1 = n := by simpa [G] using hcard
    exact_mod_cast hcN
  have hG : 2 ≤ G.card := by
    have hc : G.card + 1 = n := by simpa [G] using hcard
    omega
  have hflat := pointLoss_mul_card_sub_two_le_cost M hM G hG i S
  have heq := cost_good_eq_clean M hM bad G (by simp [G]) S
  have hmono := FTC.cost_mono (corruptContribution_nonneg M hM bad)
    (Finset.erase_subset bad Finset.univ) S
  change FTC.cost (corruptContribution M hM bad) G S ≤ _ at hmono
  rw [heq] at hmono
  have hci : corruptContribution M hM bad i S = pointLoss M hM (p i) S := by simp [hib]
  rw [hci]
  have hcoef : (G.card : ℝ) - 2 = (n : ℝ) - 3 := by linarith
  rw [hcoef] at hflat
  exact hflat.trans hmono

decl_42.name: FTC.Counterexample.corrupt_cost_lower_bound
decl_42.label: Counterexample.corrupt_cost_lower_bound
decl_42.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/FlatQueries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_42.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  3 ≤ n → ∀ (bad : Fin n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n), ↑n - 3 ≤ FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost M hM bad S
decl_42.source:
theorem corrupt_cost_lower_bound {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 3 ≤ n) (bad : Fin n) (S : Query n) :
    (n : ℝ) - 3 ≤ corruptCost M hM bad S := by
  let G := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).erase bad
  have hcard := Finset.card_erase_add_one (Finset.mem_univ bad)
  have hcardR : (G.card : ℝ) + 1 = (n : ℝ) := by
    have hcN : G.card + 1 = n := by simpa [G] using hcard
    exact_mod_cast hcN
  have hG : 2 ≤ G.card := by
    have hc : G.card + 1 = n := by simpa [G] using hcard
    omega
  have hlo := card_sub_two_le_cost M hM G hG S
  have heq := cost_good_eq_clean M hM bad G (by simp [G]) S
  have hmono := FTC.cost_mono (corruptContribution_nonneg M hM bad)
    (Finset.erase_subset bad Finset.univ) S
  change FTC.cost (corruptContribution M hM bad) G S ≤ _ at hmono
  rw [heq] at hmono
  change (n : ℝ) - 3 ≤ FTC.cost (corruptContribution M hM bad) Finset.univ S
  linarith

end FTC.Counterexample

decl_63.name: FTC.Counterexample.graphDist
decl_63.label: Counterexample.graphDist
decl_63.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_63.statement: {n : ℕ} → ℝ → FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n → FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n → ℝ
decl_63.source:
def graphDist {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) : Vertex n → Vertex n → ℝ
  | .inl i, .inl j => unitDistance i j
  | .inl i, .inr false => firstDistance i
  | .inr false, .inl i => firstDistance i
  | .inl _, .inr true => M
  | .inr true, .inl _ => M
  | .inr false, .inr true => M + 1 / 2
  | .inr true, .inr false => M + 1 / 2
  | .inr false, .inr false => 0
  | .inr true, .inr true => 0

decl_78.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (x : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n), FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M x x = 0
decl_78.source:
@[simp] theorem graphDist_self {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (x : Vertex n) :
    graphDist M x x = 0 := by
  rcases x with i | (_ | _) <;> simp [graphDist, unitDistance]

decl_70.name: FTC.Counterexample.graphDist_comm
decl_70.label: Counterexample.graphDist_comm
decl_70.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_70.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (x y : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n),
  FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M x y = FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M y x
decl_70.source:
theorem graphDist_comm {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (x y : Vertex n) :
    graphDist M x y = graphDist M y x := by
  rcases x with i | (_ | _) <;> rcases y with j | (_ | _) <;>
    simp [graphDist, unitDistance, eq_comm]

/-- The triangle inequality, proved over the finite vertex cases. -/

decl_79.name: FTC.Counterexample.graphDist_triangle
decl_79.label: Counterexample.graphDist_triangle
decl_79.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_79.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ),
  1 ≤ M →
    ∀ (x y z : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n),
      FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M x z ≤ FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M x y + FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M y z
decl_79.source:
theorem graphDist_triangle {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (x y z : Vertex n) : graphDist M x z ≤ graphDist M x y + graphDist M y z := by
  rcases x with i | (_ | _) <;>
    rcases y with j | (_ | _) <;>
      rcases z with k | (_ | _) <;>
        simp only [graphDist, unitDistance, firstDistance] <;>
          (try split_ifs) <;> (try simp_all) <;> linarith

decl_74.name: FTC.Counterexample.graphDist_nonneg
decl_74.label: Counterexample.graphDist_nonneg
decl_74.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_74.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ), 1 ≤ M → ∀ (x y : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n), 0 ≤ FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M x y
decl_74.source:
theorem graphDist_nonneg {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (x y : Vertex n) :
    0 ≤ graphDist M x y := by
  have h := graphDist_triangle M hM x y x
  rw [graphDist_self, graphDist_comm M y x] at h
  linarith

decl_72.name: FTC.Counterexample.graphDist_eq_zero_iff
decl_72.label: Counterexample.graphDist_eq_zero_iff
decl_72.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_72.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ), 1 ≤ M → ∀ (x y : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n), FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M x y = 0 ↔ x = y
decl_72.source:
theorem graphDist_eq_zero_iff {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (x y : Vertex n) :
    graphDist M x y = 0 ↔ x = y := by
  have hMne : M ≠ 0 := by linarith
  rcases x with i | (_ | _) <;> rcases y with j | (_ | _) <;>
    simp [graphDist, unitDistance, firstDistance, hMne] <;>
      (try split_ifs) <;> norm_num at * <;> linarith

/-- The actual finite metric space used in the counterexample. Install this
locally with `letI := metricSpace M hM`. -/

decl_80.name: FTC.Counterexample.metricSpace
decl_80.label: Counterexample.metricSpace
decl_80.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_80.source:
@[reducible] def metricSpace {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) : MetricSpace (Vertex n) where
  dist := graphDist M
  dist_self := graphDist_self M
  dist_comm := graphDist_comm M
  dist_triangle := graphDist_triangle M hM
  eq_of_dist_eq_zero := fun h => (graphDist_eq_zero_iff M hM _ _).mp h

decl_52.name: FTC.Counterexample.dist_metricSpace
decl_52.label: Counterexample.dist_metricSpace
decl_52.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_52.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (x y : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n), dist x y = FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M x y
decl_52.source:
@[simp] theorem dist_metricSpace {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (x y : Vertex n) :
    @dist (Vertex n) (metricSpace M hM).toDist x y = graphDist M x y := rfl

/-- The common distance from an original point to a center, outside that
center's exceptional set. -/

decl_10.name: FTC.Counterexample.baseline
decl_10.label: Counterexample.baseline
decl_10.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_10.source:
def baseline {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) : Vertex n → ℝ
  | .inl _ => 1
  | .inr false => 3 / 2
  | .inr true => M

/-- Each center has at most one exceptional original point. -/

decl_55.label: Counterexample.exceptional
decl_55.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.

decl_59.source: @[simp] theorem exceptional_p {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n) : exceptional (p i) = {i} := rfl

decl_56.name: FTC.Counterexample.exceptional_a

decl_56.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_56.source:
@[simp] theorem exceptional_a {n : ℕ} :
    exceptional (a : Vertex n) = Finset.univ.filter (fun i => i.val = 0) := rfl

decl_57.name: FTC.Counterexample.exceptional_b
decl_57.label: Counterexample.exceptional_b
decl_57.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_57.source: @[simp] theorem exceptional_b {n : ℕ} : exceptional (b : Vertex n) = ∅ := rfl

decl_58.name: FTC.Counterexample.exceptional_card_le_one
decl_58.label: Counterexample.exceptional_card_le_one
decl_58.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_58.source:
theorem exceptional_card_le_one {n : ℕ} (v : Vertex n) : (exceptional v).card ≤ 1 := by
  rcases v with i | (_ | _)
  · simp [exceptional]
  · apply Finset.card_le_one.mpr
    intro i hi j hj
    apply Fin.ext
    exact (Finset.mem_filter.mp hi).2.trans (Finset.mem_filter.mp hj).2.symm
  · simp [exceptional]

decl_81.name: FTC.Counterexample.one_le_baseline
decl_81.label: Counterexample.one_le_baseline
decl_81.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_81.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ), 1 ≤ M → ∀ (v : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n), 1 ≤ FTC.Counterexample.baseline M v
decl_81.source:
theorem one_le_baseline {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (v : Vertex n) :
    1 ≤ baseline M v := by
  rcases v with i | (_ | _) <;> simp only [baseline] <;> linarith

decl_11.name: FTC.Counterexample.baseline_nonneg
decl_11.label: Counterexample.baseline_nonneg
decl_11.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_11.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ), 1 ≤ M → ∀ (v : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n), 0 ≤ FTC.Counterexample.baseline M v
decl_11.source:
theorem baseline_nonneg {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (v : Vertex n) :
    0 ≤ baseline M v := le_trans (by norm_num) (one_le_baseline M hM v)

/-- Exceptional original points have no larger distance than the common
level of a center. -/

decl_73.name: FTC.Counterexample.graphDist_le_baseline
decl_73.label: Counterexample.graphDist_le_baseline
decl_73.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_73.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (i : Fin n) (v : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n),
  FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M (FTC.Counterexample.p i) v ≤ FTC.Counterexample.baseline M v
decl_73.source:
theorem graphDist_le_baseline {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (i : Fin n) (v : Vertex n) :
    graphDist M (p i) v ≤ baseline M v := by
  rcases v with j | (_ | _)
  · exact unitDistance_le_one i j
  · exact (firstDistance_bounds i).2
  · exact le_rfl

/-- Outside its at-most-one exception, a center has exactly its common
original-point distance. -/

decl_71.name: FTC.Counterexample.graphDist_eq_baseline_of_notMem
decl_71.label: Counterexample.graphDist_eq_baseline_of_notMem
decl_71.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Metric.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_71.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (i : Fin n) (v : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n),
  i ∉ FTC.Counterexample.exceptional v →
    FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M (FTC.Counterexample.p i) v = FTC.Counterexample.baseline M v
decl_71.source:
theorem graphDist_eq_baseline_of_notMem {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (i : Fin n) (v : Vertex n)
    (hi : i ∉ exceptional v) : graphDist M (p i) v = baseline M v := by
  rcases v with j | (_ | _)
  · have hij : i ≠ j := by simpa [exceptional] using hi
    simp [graphDist, unitDistance, baseline, hij]
  · have hi0 : i.val ≠ 0 := by simpa [exceptional] using hi
    simp [graphDist, firstDistance, baseline, hi0]
  · rfl

end

end FTC.Counterexample

decl_28.name: FTC.Counterexample.clusterMembers

decl_28.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyCore.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.

decl_28.source:
def clusterMembers {n : ℕ} (first i : Fin n) : Finset (Fin n) :=

decl_13.name: FTC.Counterexample.card_cluster_first
decl_13.label: Counterexample.card_cluster_first
decl_13.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyCore.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_13.source:

decl_14.name: FTC.Counterexample.card_cluster_other
decl_14.label: Counterexample.card_cluster_other
decl_14.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyCore.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_14.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ} (first i : Fin n), i ≠ first → ↑(FTC.Counterexample.clusterMembers first i).card = ↑n - 1
decl_14.source:
theorem card_cluster_other {n : ℕ} (first i : Fin n) (hi : i ≠ first) :
    ((clusterMembers first i).card : ℝ) = (n : ℝ) - 1 := by
  have h := Finset.card_erase_add_one (Finset.mem_univ first)
  have hR : (((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).erase first).card : ℝ) + 1 = (n : ℝ) := by
    have hN : (((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).erase first).card) + 1 = n := by simpa using h
    exact_mod_cast hN
  simp only [clusterMembers, if_neg hi]
  linarith

/-- The usual proxy, with exactly the scaling used in Appendix A.1. -/

decl_100.name: FTC.Counterexample.proxy
decl_100.label: Counterexample.proxy
decl_100.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyCore.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_100.statement: {n : ℕ} → (M : ℝ) → 1 ≤ M → Fin n → Fin n → FTC.Counterexample.Query n → Fin n → ℝ
decl_100.source:
noncomputable def proxy {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad first : Fin n) (A : Query n) (i : Fin n) : ℝ :=
  2 / ((clusterMembers first i).card : ℝ) +
    2 * corruptContribution M hM bad i A / corruptCost M hM bad A

decl_103.name: FTC.Counterexample.proxy_first
decl_103.label: Counterexample.proxy_first
decl_103.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyCore.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_103.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (bad first : Fin n) (A : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
  FTC.Counterexample.proxy M hM bad first A first =
    2 + 2 * FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad first A / FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost M hM bad A
decl_103.source:
theorem proxy_first {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad first : Fin n) (A : Query n) :
    proxy M hM bad first A first =
      2 + 2 * corruptContribution M hM bad first A / corruptCost M hM bad A := by
  simp [proxy]

decl_106.name: FTC.Counterexample.proxy_other
decl_106.label: Counterexample.proxy_other
decl_106.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyCore.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_106.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (bad first i : Fin n) (A : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
  i ≠ first →
    FTC.Counterexample.proxy M hM bad first A i =
      2 / (↑n - 1) + 2 * FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad i A / FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost M hM bad A
decl_106.source:
theorem proxy_other {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad first i : Fin n) (A : Query n) (hi : i ≠ first) :
    proxy M hM bad first A i =
      2 / ((n : ℝ) - 1) +
        2 * corruptContribution M hM bad i A / corruptCost M hM bad A := by
  rw [proxy, card_cluster_other first i hi]

decl_30.name: FTC.Counterexample.cluster_term_le_proxy
decl_30.label: Counterexample.cluster_term_le_proxy
decl_30.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyCore.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_30.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (bad first i : Fin n) (A : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
  2 / ↑(FTC.Counterexample.clusterMembers first i).card ≤ FTC.Counterexample.proxy M hM bad first A i
decl_30.source:
theorem cluster_term_le_proxy {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad first i : Fin n) (A : Query n) :
    2 / ((clusterMembers first i).card : ℝ) ≤ proxy M hM bad first A i := by
  have hc : 0 ≤ corruptCost M hM bad A :=
    FTC.cost_nonneg (corruptContribution_nonneg M hM bad) _ _
  have hsecond : 0 ≤ 2 * corruptContribution M hM bad i A / corruptCost M hM bad A :=
    div_nonneg (mul_nonneg (by norm_num) (corruptContribution_nonneg M hM bad i A)) hc
  unfold proxy
  linarith

/-- Ties elsewhere do not matter when the maximizing entry is strict. This
identifies the output of the actual Algorithm 1 function. -/

decl_85.name: FTC.Counterexample.peel_one_of_strict_max
decl_85.label: Counterexample.peel_one_of_strict_max
decl_85.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyCore.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_85.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq I] (score : Finset I → I → ℝ) (U : Finset I),
  ∀ x ∈ U, (∀ i ∈ U, i ≠ x → score U i < score U x) → FTC.peel score 1 U = U.erase x
decl_85.source:
theorem peel_one_of_strict_max {I : Type*} [DecidableEq I]
    (score : Finset I → I → ℝ) (U : Finset I) (x : I)
    (hx : x ∈ U) (hstrict : ∀ i ∈ U, i ≠ x → score U i < score U x) :
    FTC.peel score 1 U = U.erase x := by
  have hU : U.Nonempty := ⟨x, hx⟩
  have hspec := FTC.chosenMax_spec score U hU
  have hchosen : FTC.chosenMax score U hU = x := by
    by_contra h
    exact (not_lt_of_ge (hspec.2 x hx)) (hstrict _ hspec.1 h)
  simp [FTC.peel, FTC.peelStep, hU, hchosen]

end FTC.Counterexample

decl_8.name: FTC.Counterexample.assignedCenter
decl_8.label: Counterexample.assignedCenter
decl_8.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyReference.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_8.statement: {n : ℕ} → Fin n → Fin n → Fin n → FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n
decl_8.source:
def assignedCenter {n : ℕ} (first j i : Fin n) : Vertex n := if i = first then a else p j

/-- The proxy clusters are exactly the fibers of the reference assignment. -/

decl_29.name: FTC.Counterexample.clusterMembers_eq_assignment_fiber
decl_29.label: Counterexample.clusterMembers_eq_assignment_fiber
decl_29.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyReference.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_29.source:
theorem clusterMembers_eq_assignment_fiber {n : ℕ} (first j i : Fin n) :
    clusterMembers first i = Finset.univ.filter
      (fun z => assignedCenter first j z = assignedCenter first j i) := by
  ext z
  by_cases hi : i = first <;> by_cases hz : z = first <;>
    simp [clusterMembers, assignedCenter, hi, hz]

/-- Every reference assignment is the unique closest of its two centers. -/

decl_114.name: FTC.Counterexample.reference_assignment_nearest
decl_114.label: Counterexample.reference_assignment_nearest
decl_114.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyReference.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_114.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (bad first j : Fin n),
  ↑first = 0 →
    ↑j ≠ 0 →
      ↑bad ≠ 0 →
        ∀ (i : Fin n),
          if i = first then
            FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M (FTC.Counterexample.corruptedEntries bad i).point FTC.Counterexample.a <
              FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M (FTC.Counterexample.corruptedEntries bad i).point (FTC.Counterexample.p j)
          else
            FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M (FTC.Counterexample.corruptedEntries bad i).point (FTC.Counterexample.p j) <
              FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M (FTC.Counterexample.corruptedEntries bad i).point FTC.Counterexample.a
decl_114.source:
theorem reference_assignment_nearest {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ)
    (bad first j : Fin n) (hfirst : first.val = 0) (hj : j.val ≠ 0)
    (hbad : bad.val ≠ 0) (i : Fin n) :
    if i = first then
      graphDist M (corruptedEntries bad i).point a <
        graphDist M (corruptedEntries bad i).point (p j)
    else graphDist M (corruptedEntries bad i).point (p j) <
        graphDist M (corruptedEntries bad i).point a := by
  have hfb : first ≠ bad := by intro h; exact hbad (h ▸ hfirst)
  by_cases hi : i = first
  · subst i
    simpa [corruptedEntries, hfb] using reference_first_nearest M first j hfirst hj
  · rw [if_neg hi]
    by_cases hib : i = bad
    · subst i
      simpa [corruptedEntries] using reference_b_nearest M j
    · have hi0 : i.val ≠ 0 := by
        intro h0
        apply hi
        exact Fin.ext (h0.trans hfirst.symm)
      simpa [corruptedEntries, hib] using reference_other_nearest M i j hi0

decl_116.name: FTC.Counterexample.reference_cost_formula
decl_116.label: Counterexample.reference_cost_formula
decl_116.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyReference.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_116.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  M ^ 2 = ↑n - 4 →
    ∀ (bad first j : Fin n),
      ↑first = 0 →
        ↑j ≠ 0 →
          ↑bad ≠ 0 →
            bad ≠ j →
              FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost M hM bad (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) =
                FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.referenceCost ↑n
decl_116.source:
theorem reference_cost_formula {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4) (bad first j : Fin n)
    (hfirst : first.val = 0) (hj : j.val ≠ 0) (hbad : bad.val ≠ 0) (hbj : bad ≠ j) :
    corruptCost M hM bad (referenceQuery j) = referenceCost (n : ℝ) := by
  rw [corruptCost_reference M hM bad first j hfirst hj hbad hbj, hM2]
  unfold referenceCost
  ring

/-- The reference centers really are a factor-two approximation on Q. -/

decl_118.name: FTC.Counterexample.reference_is_two_approx
decl_118.label: Counterexample.reference_is_two_approx
decl_118.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyReference.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_118.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  8 ≤ n →
    M ^ 2 = ↑n - 4 →
      ∀ (bad first j : Fin n),
        ↑first = 0 →
          ↑j ≠ 0 →
            ↑bad ≠ 0 →
              bad ≠ j →
                ∀ (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
                  FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost M hM bad (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) ≤
                    2 * FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost M hM bad S
decl_118.source:
theorem reference_is_two_approx {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 8 ≤ n) (hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4) (bad first j : Fin n)
    (hfirst : first.val = 0) (hj : j.val ≠ 0) (hbad : bad.val ≠ 0) (hbj : bad ≠ j)
    (S : Query n) : corruptCost M hM bad (referenceQuery j) ≤ 2 * corruptCost M hM bad S := by
  rw [reference_cost_formula M hM hM2 bad first j hfirst hj hbad hbj]
  exact reference_two_approx (corrupt_cost_lower_bound M hM (by omega) bad S)

decl_104.name: FTC.Counterexample.proxy_first_formula
decl_104.label: Counterexample.proxy_first_formula
decl_104.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyReference.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_104.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  8 ≤ n →
    M ^ 2 = ↑n - 4 →
      ∀ (bad first j : Fin n),
        ↑first = 0 →
          ↑j ≠ 0 →
            ↑bad ≠ 0 →
              bad ≠ j →
                FTC.Counterexample.proxy M hM bad first (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) first =
                  FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.singletonProxy ↑n
decl_104.source:
theorem proxy_first_formula {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 8 ≤ n) (hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4) (bad first j : Fin n)
    (hfirst : first.val = 0) (hj : j.val ≠ 0) (hbad : bad.val ≠ 0) (hbj : bad ≠ j) :
    proxy M hM bad first (referenceQuery j) first = singletonProxy (n : ℝ) := by
  have hfb : first ≠ bad := by intro h; exact hbad (h ▸ hfirst)
  rw [proxy_first, corruptContribution_apply, if_neg hfb,
    pointLoss_first_reference M hM first j hfirst hj,
    reference_cost_formula M hM hM2 bad first j hfirst hj hbad hbj]
  have hnR : (8 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have hd := referenceCost_pos hnR
  unfold singletonProxy
  field_simp [ne_of_gt hd]
  <;> ring

decl_102.name: FTC.Counterexample.proxy_bad_formula
decl_102.label: Counterexample.proxy_bad_formula
decl_102.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyReference.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_102.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  M ^ 2 = ↑n - 4 →
    ∀ (bad first j : Fin n),
      ↑first = 0 →
        ↑j ≠ 0 →
          ↑bad ≠ 0 →
            bad ≠ j →
              FTC.Counterexample.proxy M hM bad first (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) bad =
                FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionProxy ↑n
decl_102.source:
theorem proxy_bad_formula {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4) (bad first j : Fin n)
    (hfirst : first.val = 0) (hj : j.val ≠ 0) (hbad : bad.val ≠ 0) (hbj : bad ≠ j) :
    proxy M hM bad first (referenceQuery j) bad = corruptionProxy (n : ℝ) := by
  have hbf : bad ≠ first := by intro h; exact hbad (h.symm ▸ hfirst)
  rw [proxy_other M hM bad first bad (referenceQuery j) hbf,
    corruptContribution_apply, if_pos rfl, pointLoss_b_reference,
    reference_cost_formula M hM hM2 bad first j hfirst hj hbad hbj, hM2]
  rfl

decl_105.name: FTC.Counterexample.proxy_ordinary_le
decl_105.label: Counterexample.proxy_ordinary_le
decl_105.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyReference.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_105.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  8 ≤ n →
    M ^ 2 = ↑n - 4 →
      ∀ (bad first j i : Fin n),
        ↑first = 0 →
          ↑j ≠ 0 →
            ↑bad ≠ 0 →
              bad ≠ j →
                i ≠ first →
                  i ≠ bad →
                    FTC.Counterexample.proxy M hM bad first (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) i ≤
                      FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.ordinaryProxy ↑n
decl_105.source:
theorem proxy_ordinary_le {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 8 ≤ n) (hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4) (bad first j i : Fin n)
    (hfirst : first.val = 0) (hj : j.val ≠ 0) (hbad : bad.val ≠ 0) (hbj : bad ≠ j)
    (hif : i ≠ first) (hib : i ≠ bad) :
    proxy M hM bad first (referenceQuery j) i ≤ ordinaryProxy (n : ℝ) := by
  rw [proxy_other M hM bad first i (referenceQuery j) hif,
    corruptContribution_apply, if_neg hib,
    reference_cost_formula M hM hM2 bad first j hfirst hj hbad hbj]
  have hnR : (8 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have hd := referenceCost_pos hnR
  have hcap := pointLoss_reference_le_one M hM i j
  have hr : 2 * pointLoss M hM (p i) (referenceQuery j) / referenceCost (n : ℝ) ≤
      2 / referenceCost (n : ℝ) := by
    apply div_le_div_of_nonneg_right _ hd.le
    linarith
  unfold ordinaryProxy
  linarith

/-- The singleton uniquely maximizes the proxy, although it is genuine. -/

decl_110.name: FTC.Counterexample.proxy_strict_max
decl_110.label: Counterexample.proxy_strict_max
decl_110.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyReference.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_110.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  8 ≤ n →
    M ^ 2 = ↑n - 4 →
      ∀ (bad first j i : Fin n),
        ↑first = 0 →
          ↑j ≠ 0 →
            ↑bad ≠ 0 →
              bad ≠ j →
                i ≠ first →
                  FTC.Counterexample.proxy M hM bad first (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) i <
                    FTC.Counterexample.proxy M hM bad first (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) first
decl_110.source:
theorem proxy_strict_max {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 8 ≤ n) (hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4) (bad first j i : Fin n)
    (hfirst : first.val = 0) (hj : j.val ≠ 0) (hbad : bad.val ≠ 0) (hbj : bad ≠ j)
    (hif : i ≠ first) :
    proxy M hM bad first (referenceQuery j) i <
      proxy M hM bad first (referenceQuery j) first := by
  have hnR : (8 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  rw [proxy_first_formula M hM hn hM2 bad first j hfirst hj hbad hbj]
  by_cases hib : i = bad
  · subst i
    rw [proxy_bad_formula M hM hM2 bad first j hfirst hj hbad hbj]
    exact (corruptionProxy_lt_two hnR).trans (singletonProxy_gt_two hnR)
  · exact ((proxy_ordinary_le M hM hn hM2 bad first j i hfirst hj hbad hbj hif hib).trans_lt
      (ordinaryProxy_lt_two hnR)).trans (singletonProxy_gt_two hnR)

/-- These are valid pointwise sensitivity upper bounds on the actual Q. -/

decl_120.name: FTC.Counterexample.sensitivity_le_proxy
decl_120.label: Counterexample.sensitivity_le_proxy
decl_120.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/ProxyReference.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_120.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  8 ≤ n →
    M ^ 2 = ↑n - 4 →
      ∀ (bad first j i : Fin n),
        ↑first = 0 →
          ↑j ≠ 0 →
            ↑bad ≠ 0 →
              bad ≠ j →
                FTC.sensitivity (FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad) Finset.univ i ≤
                  FTC.Counterexample.proxy M hM bad first (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) i
decl_120.source:
theorem sensitivity_le_proxy {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 8 ≤ n) (hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4) (bad first j i : Fin n)
    (hfirst : first.val = 0) (hj : j.val ≠ 0) (hbad : bad.val ≠ 0) (hbj : bad ≠ j) :
    FTC.sensitivity (corruptContribution M hM bad) Finset.univ i ≤
      proxy M hM bad first (referenceQuery j) i := by
  have hnR : (8 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  by_cases hib : i = bad
  · subst i
    rw [proxy_bad_formula M hM hM2 bad first j hfirst hj hbad hbj]
    exact (FTC.sensitivity_le_one (corruptContribution_nonneg M hM bad) _ _).trans
      (corruptionProxy_gt_one hnR).le
  · by_cases hif : i = first
    · subst i
      rw [proxy_first_formula M hM hn hM2 bad first j hfirst hj hbad hbj]
      exact (FTC.sensitivity_le_one (corruptContribution_nonneg M hM bad) _ _).trans
        (by linarith [singletonProxy_gt_two hnR])
    · have hterm := cluster_term_le_proxy M hM bad first i (referenceQuery j)
      rw [card_cluster_other first i hif] at hterm
      exact (corrupt_good_sensitivity_le M hM (by omega) bad i hib).trans
        ((genuineBound_le_cluster_term hnR).trans hterm)

end FTC.Counterexample

decl_91.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_eq_inf
decl_91.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_eq_inf
decl_91.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_91.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (x : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
  FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM x S = S.centers.inf' ⋯ fun y => FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M x y ^ 2

    (x : Vertex n) (S : Query n) :

decl_95.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_nonneg
decl_95.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_nonneg
decl_95.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.

∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (x : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),

theorem pointLoss_nonneg {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (x : Vertex n) (S : Query n) : 0 ≤ pointLoss M hM x S := by
  rw [pointLoss_eq_inf]
  apply Finset.le_inf'
  intro y _
  exact sq_nonneg _

decl_97.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_pair
decl_97.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_pair
decl_97.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_97.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (z x y : FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n) (hxy : x ≠ y),
  FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM z (FTC.Counterexample.pairQuery x y hxy) =
    min (FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M z x ^ 2) (FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M z y ^ 2)
decl_97.source:
@[simp] theorem pointLoss_pair {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (z x y : Vertex n) (hxy : x ≠ y) :
    pointLoss M hM z (pairQuery x y hxy) =
      min (graphDist M z x ^ 2) (graphDist M z y ^ 2) := by
  rw [pointLoss_eq_inf]
  apply le_antisymm
  · apply le_min
    · exact Finset.inf'_le _ (by simp [pairQuery])
    · exact Finset.inf'_le _ (by simp [pairQuery])
  · apply Finset.le_inf'
    intro v hv
    simp only [pairQuery, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton] at hv
    rcases hv with rfl | rfl
    · exact min_le_left _ _
    · exact min_le_right _ _

/-- The clean coreset is the whole input, with one separately indexed unit
entry at each original point. -/

decl_22.name: FTC.Counterexample.cleanEntries
decl_22.label: Counterexample.cleanEntries
decl_22.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_22.source:
def cleanEntries {n : ℕ} (i : Fin n) : FTC.Entry (Vertex n) where
  point := p i
  weight := 1
  weight_nonneg := by norm_num

/-- Move just the entry with index `bad` to `b`; keep its unit weight. -/

decl_46.name: FTC.Counterexample.corruptedEntries
decl_46.label: Counterexample.corruptedEntries
decl_46.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_46.statement: {n : ℕ} → Fin n → Fin n → FTC.Entry (FTC.Counterexample.Vertex n)
decl_46.source:
def corruptedEntries {n : ℕ} (bad i : Fin n) : FTC.Entry (Vertex n) where
  point := if i = bad then b else p i
  weight := 1
  weight_nonneg := by norm_num

decl_16.name: FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution
decl_16.label: Counterexample.cleanContribution
decl_16.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_16.statement: {n : ℕ} → (M : ℝ) → 1 ≤ M → Fin n → FTC.Counterexample.Query n → ℝ
decl_16.source:
noncomputable def cleanContribution {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (i : Fin n) (S : Query n) : ℝ :=
  FTC.contribution (pointLoss M hM) cleanEntries i S

decl_35.name: FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution
decl_35.label: Counterexample.corruptContribution
decl_35.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_35.statement: {n : ℕ} → (M : ℝ) → 1 ≤ M → Fin n → Fin n → FTC.Counterexample.Query n → ℝ

noncomputable def corruptContribution {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
