decl_17.name: FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution_apply
decl_17.label: Counterexample.cleanContribution_apply
decl_17.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_17.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (i : Fin n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
  FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution M hM i S = FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM (FTC.Counterexample.p i) S
decl_17.source:
@[simp] theorem cleanContribution_apply {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (i : Fin n) (S : Query n) : cleanContribution M hM i S = pointLoss M hM (p i) S := by
  simp [cleanContribution, FTC.contribution, cleanEntries]

decl_36.name: FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution_apply
decl_36.label: Counterexample.corruptContribution_apply
decl_36.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_36.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (bad i : Fin n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
  FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad i S =
    if i = bad then FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM FTC.Counterexample.b S
    else FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM (FTC.Counterexample.p i) S
decl_36.source:
@[simp] theorem corruptContribution_apply {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad i : Fin n) (S : Query n) :
    corruptContribution M hM bad i S =
      if i = bad then pointLoss M hM b S else pointLoss M hM (p i) S := by
  by_cases hi : i = bad <;> simp [corruptContribution, FTC.contribution, corruptedEntries, hi]

decl_19.name: FTC.Counterexample.cleanCost
decl_19.label: Counterexample.cleanCost
decl_19.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_19.statement: {n : ℕ} → (M : ℝ) → 1 ≤ M → FTC.Counterexample.Query n → ℝ
decl_19.source:
noncomputable def cleanCost {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (S : Query n) : ℝ :=
  FTC.cost (cleanContribution M hM) Finset.univ S

decl_38.name: FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost
decl_38.label: Counterexample.corruptCost
decl_38.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_38.statement: {n : ℕ} → (M : ℝ) → 1 ≤ M → Fin n → FTC.Counterexample.Query n → ℝ
decl_38.source:
noncomputable def corruptCost {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad : Fin n) (S : Query n) : ℝ :=
  FTC.cost (corruptContribution M hM bad) Finset.univ S

decl_18.name: FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution_nonneg
decl_18.label: Counterexample.cleanContribution_nonneg
decl_18.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_18.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (i : Fin n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
  0 ≤ FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution M hM i S
decl_18.source:
theorem cleanContribution_nonneg {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (i : Fin n) (S : Query n) : 0 ≤ cleanContribution M hM i S := by
  simp only [cleanContribution_apply]
  exact pointLoss_nonneg M hM _ _

decl_37.name: FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution_nonneg
decl_37.label: Counterexample.corruptContribution_nonneg
decl_37.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Queries.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_37.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (bad i : Fin n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
  0 ≤ FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad i S
decl_37.source:
theorem corruptContribution_nonneg {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad i : Fin n) (S : Query n) : 0 ≤ corruptContribution M hM bad i S := by
  simp only [corruptContribution_apply]
  split_ifs <;> exact pointLoss_nonneg M hM _ _

end FTC.Counterexample

decl_23.name: FTC.Counterexample.clean_entry_bound
decl_23.label: Counterexample.clean_entry_bound
decl_23.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/SensitivityBounds.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_23.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  3 ≤ n →
    ∀ (i : Fin n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
      FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution M hM i S ≤ 1 / (↑n - 2) * FTC.Counterexample.cleanCost M hM S
decl_23.source:
theorem clean_entry_bound {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 3 ≤ n) (i : Fin n) (S : Query n) :
    cleanContribution M hM i S ≤ (1 / ((n : ℝ) - 2)) * cleanCost M hM S := by
  have hnR : (3 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have hd : 0 < (n : ℝ) - 2 := by linarith
  have h := clean_uniform_bound M hM (by omega) i S
  calc
    cleanContribution M hM i S ≤ cleanCost M hM S / ((n : ℝ) - 2) :=
      (le_div_iff₀ hd).2 (by nlinarith [h])
    _ = (1 / ((n : ℝ) - 2)) * cleanCost M hM S := by ring

decl_26.name: FTC.Counterexample.clean_sensitivity_le
decl_26.label: Counterexample.clean_sensitivity_le
decl_26.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/SensitivityBounds.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_26.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  3 ≤ n → ∀ (i : Fin n), FTC.sensitivity (FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution M hM) Finset.univ i ≤ 1 / (↑n - 2)
decl_26.source:
theorem clean_sensitivity_le {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 3 ≤ n) (i : Fin n) :
    FTC.sensitivity (cleanContribution M hM) Finset.univ i ≤ 1 / ((n : ℝ) - 2) := by
  have hnR : (3 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  apply FTC.sensitivity_le_of_contribution_le (cleanContribution_nonneg M hM)
    (Finset.mem_univ i) (div_nonneg (by norm_num) (by linarith))
  exact clean_entry_bound M hM hn i

decl_43.name: FTC.Counterexample.corrupt_good_entry_bound
decl_43.label: Counterexample.corrupt_good_entry_bound
decl_43.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/SensitivityBounds.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_43.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  4 ≤ n →
    ∀ (bad i : Fin n),
      i ≠ bad →
        ∀ (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
          FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad i S ≤ 1 / (↑n - 3) * FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost M hM bad S
decl_43.source:
theorem corrupt_good_entry_bound {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 4 ≤ n) (bad i : Fin n) (hib : i ≠ bad) (S : Query n) :
    corruptContribution M hM bad i S ≤
      (1 / ((n : ℝ) - 3)) * corruptCost M hM bad S := by
  have hnR : (4 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have hd : 0 < (n : ℝ) - 3 := by linarith
  have h := corrupt_uniform_good_bound M hM (by omega) bad i hib S
  calc
    corruptContribution M hM bad i S ≤ corruptCost M hM bad S / ((n : ℝ) - 3) :=
      (le_div_iff₀ hd).2 (by nlinarith [h])
    _ = (1 / ((n : ℝ) - 3)) * corruptCost M hM bad S := by ring

decl_44.name: FTC.Counterexample.corrupt_good_sensitivity_le
decl_44.label: Counterexample.corrupt_good_sensitivity_le
decl_44.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/SensitivityBounds.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_44.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  4 ≤ n →
    ∀ (bad i : Fin n),
      i ≠ bad → FTC.sensitivity (FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad) Finset.univ i ≤ 1 / (↑n - 3)
decl_44.source:
theorem corrupt_good_sensitivity_le {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 4 ≤ n) (bad i : Fin n) (hib : i ≠ bad) :
    FTC.sensitivity (corruptContribution M hM bad) Finset.univ i ≤
      1 / ((n : ℝ) - 3) := by
  have hnR : (4 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  apply FTC.sensitivity_le_of_contribution_le (corruptContribution_nonneg M hM bad)
    (Finset.mem_univ i) (div_nonneg (by norm_num) (by linarith))
  exact corrupt_good_entry_bound M hM hn bad i hib

/-- Removing the corruption yields an ε-coreset: only the one original clean
copy at its former location is missing. -/

decl_53.name: FTC.Counterexample.exact_deletion_isCoreset
decl_53.label: Counterexample.exact_deletion_isCoreset
decl_53.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/SensitivityBounds.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_53.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  3 ≤ n →
    ∀ (bad : Fin n) (ε : ℝ),
      0 ≤ ε →
        1 / (↑n - 2) ≤ ε →
          FTC.IsCoreset ε (FTC.Counterexample.cleanCost M hM)
            (FTC.cost (FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad) (Finset.univ.erase bad))
decl_53.source:
theorem exact_deletion_isCoreset {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 3 ≤ n) (bad : Fin n) (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
    (hsmall : 1 / ((n : ℝ) - 2) ≤ ε) :
    FTC.IsCoreset ε (cleanCost M hM)
      (FTC.cost (corruptContribution M hM bad) (Finset.univ.erase bad)) := by
  intro S
  have heq := cost_good_eq_clean M hM bad (Finset.univ.erase bad) (by simp) S
  rw [heq]
  have hc : 0 ≤ cleanCost M hM S := FTC.cost_nonneg (cleanContribution_nonneg M hM) _ _
  have hci : 0 ≤ cleanContribution M hM bad S := cleanContribution_nonneg M hM bad S
  have hentry := clean_entry_bound M hM hn bad S
  have hbudget := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hsmall hc
  have herase := FTC.cost_erase_add (cleanContribution M hM) (Finset.mem_univ bad) S
  change FTC.cost (cleanContribution M hM) (Finset.univ.erase bad) S +
    cleanContribution M hM bad S = cleanCost M hM S at herase
  constructor <;> nlinarith

end FTC.Counterexample

decl_60.name: FTC.Counterexample.exists_two_other_indices
decl_60.label: Counterexample.exists_two_other_indices
decl_60.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/SensitivityWitnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_60.statement: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 3 ≤ n → ∀ (i : Fin n), ∃ j l, j ≠ l ∧ i ≠ j ∧ i ≠ l
decl_60.source:
theorem exists_two_other_indices {n : ℕ} (hn : 3 ≤ n) (i : Fin n) :
    ∃ j l : Fin n, j ≠ l ∧ i ≠ j ∧ i ≠ l := by
  have hc := Finset.card_erase_add_one (Finset.mem_univ i)
  have hG : 1 < ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).erase i).card := by
    simp only [Finset.card_univ, Fintype.card_fin] at hc
    omega
  obtain ⟨j, l, hj, hl, hjl⟩ := Finset.one_lt_card_iff.mp hG
  exact ⟨j, l, hjl, Ne.symm (Finset.mem_erase.mp hj).1,
    Ne.symm (Finset.mem_erase.mp hl).1⟩

/-- Every clean entry has exactly the sensitivity asserted in Appendix A.1. -/

decl_25.name: FTC.Counterexample.clean_sensitivity_eq
decl_25.label: Counterexample.clean_sensitivity_eq
decl_25.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/SensitivityWitnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_25.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  3 ≤ n → ∀ (i : Fin n), FTC.sensitivity (FTC.Counterexample.cleanContribution M hM) Finset.univ i = 1 / (↑n - 2)
decl_25.source:
theorem clean_sensitivity_eq {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 3 ≤ n) (i : Fin n) :
    FTC.sensitivity (cleanContribution M hM) Finset.univ i = 1 / ((n : ℝ) - 2) := by
  apply le_antisymm (clean_sensitivity_le M hM hn i)
  obtain ⟨j, l, hjl, hij, hil⟩ := exists_two_other_indices hn i
  have h := FTC.contribution_le_sensitivity_mul_cost (cleanContribution_nonneg M hM)
    (Finset.mem_univ i) (simplexQuery j l hjl)
  have hci : cleanContribution M hM i (simplexQuery j l hjl) = 1 := by
    rw [cleanContribution_apply, pointLoss_simplex, if_neg hij, if_neg hil]
  change _ ≤ _ * cleanCost M hM (simplexQuery j l hjl) at h
  rw [hci, cleanCost_simplex] at h
  have hnR : (3 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  apply (div_le_iff₀ (by linarith : 0 < (n : ℝ) - 2)).2
  simpa [mul_comm] using h

decl_48.name: FTC.Counterexample.corruption_sensitivity_lower
decl_48.label: Counterexample.corruption_sensitivity_lower
decl_48.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/SensitivityWitnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_48.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  4 ≤ n →
    ∀ (bad j l : Fin n),
      j ≠ l →
        bad ≠ j →
          bad ≠ l →
            M ^ 2 / (↑n - 3 + M ^ 2) ≤ FTC.sensitivity (FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad) Finset.univ bad
decl_48.source:
theorem corruption_sensitivity_lower {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 4 ≤ n) (bad j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l) (hbj : bad ≠ j) (hbl : bad ≠ l) :
    M ^ 2 / ((n : ℝ) - 3 + M ^ 2) ≤
      FTC.sensitivity (corruptContribution M hM bad) Finset.univ bad := by
  have h := FTC.contribution_le_sensitivity_mul_cost (corruptContribution_nonneg M hM bad)
    (Finset.mem_univ bad) (simplexQuery j l hjl)
  change _ ≤ _ * corruptCost M hM bad (simplexQuery j l hjl) at h
  simp only [corruptContribution_apply, if_pos rfl, pointLoss_b_simplex] at h
  rw [corruptCost_simplex M hM bad j l hjl hbj hbl] at h
  have hnR : (4 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  apply (div_le_iff₀ (by nlinarith [sq_nonneg M] : 0 < (n : ℝ) - 3 + M ^ 2)).2
  simpa [mul_comm] using h

/-- Exact sensitivity strictly prefers the corruption to every genuine entry. -/

decl_49.name: FTC.Counterexample.corruption_strict_sensitivity_max
decl_49.label: Counterexample.corruption_strict_sensitivity_max
decl_49.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/SensitivityWitnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_49.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M),
  8 ≤ n →
    M ^ 2 = ↑n - 4 →
      ∀ (bad j l : Fin n),
        j ≠ l →
          bad ≠ j →
            bad ≠ l →
              ∀ (i : Fin n),
                i ≠ bad →
                  FTC.sensitivity (FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad) Finset.univ i <
                    FTC.sensitivity (FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad) Finset.univ bad
decl_49.source:
theorem corruption_strict_sensitivity_max {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (hn : 8 ≤ n) (hM2 : M ^ 2 = (n : ℝ) - 4)
    (bad j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l) (hbj : bad ≠ j) (hbl : bad ≠ l)
    (i : Fin n) (hib : i ≠ bad) :
    FTC.sensitivity (corruptContribution M hM bad) Finset.univ i <
      FTC.sensitivity (corruptContribution M hM bad) Finset.univ bad := by
  have hnR : (8 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hn
  have hlo := corruption_sensitivity_lower M hM (by omega) bad j l hjl hbj hbl
  have hden : (n : ℝ) - 3 + M ^ 2 = 2 * (n : ℝ) - 7 := by rw [hM2]; ring
  rw [hden, hM2] at hlo
  exact (corrupt_good_sensitivity_le M hM (by omega) bad i hib).trans_lt
    ((FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.genuineBound_lt_corruptionWitness hnR).trans_le hlo)

end FTC.Counterexample

decl_121.name: FTC.Counterexample.simplexQuery
decl_121.label: Counterexample.simplexQuery
decl_121.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_121.statement: {n : ℕ} → (j l : Fin n) → j ≠ l → FTC.Counterexample.Query n

decl_113.name: FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery
decl_113.label: Counterexample.referenceQuery
decl_113.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_113.source:
def referenceQuery {n : ℕ} (j : Fin n) : Query n :=
  pairQuery a (p j) (by simp)

decl_99.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_simplex
decl_99.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_simplex
decl_99.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_99.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (i j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l),
  FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM (FTC.Counterexample.p i) (FTC.Counterexample.simplexQuery j l hjl) =
    if i = j then 0 else if i = l then 0 else 1
decl_99.source:
@[simp] theorem pointLoss_simplex {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (i j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l) :
    pointLoss M hM (p i) (simplexQuery j l hjl) =
      if i = j then 0 else if i = l then 0 else 1 := by
  rw [simplexQuery, pointLoss_pair]
  by_cases hij : i = j <;> by_cases hil : i = l <;>
    norm_num [graphDist, unitDistance, hij, hil, hjl, Ne.symm hjl]

decl_88.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_b_simplex
decl_88.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_b_simplex
decl_88.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_88.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l),
  FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM FTC.Counterexample.b (FTC.Counterexample.simplexQuery j l hjl) = M ^ 2
decl_88.source:
@[simp] theorem pointLoss_b_simplex {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l) :
    pointLoss M hM b (simplexQuery j l hjl) = M ^ 2 := by
  rw [simplexQuery, pointLoss_pair]
  simp only [graphDist_b_p, min_self]

/-- The singleton's reference-query loss is exactly `1/4`. -/

decl_92.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_first_reference
decl_92.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_first_reference
decl_92.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_92.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (first j : Fin n),
  ↑first = 0 →
    ↑j ≠ 0 →
      FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM (FTC.Counterexample.p first) (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) = 1 / 4
decl_92.source:
theorem pointLoss_first_reference {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (first j : Fin n) (hfirst : first.val = 0) (hj : j.val ≠ 0) :
    pointLoss M hM (p first) (referenceQuery j) = 1 / 4 := by
  have hfj : first ≠ j := by
    intro h
    exact hj (h ▸ hfirst)
  rw [referenceQuery, pointLoss_pair]
  norm_num [graphDist, firstDistance, unitDistance, hfirst, hfj]

/-- The other genuine noncenter points have unit reference-query loss. -/

decl_96.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_other_reference
decl_96.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_other_reference
decl_96.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_96.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (i j : Fin n),
  ↑i ≠ 0 → i ≠ j → FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM (FTC.Counterexample.p i) (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) = 1
decl_96.source:
theorem pointLoss_other_reference {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (i j : Fin n) (hi : i.val ≠ 0) (hij : i ≠ j) :
    pointLoss M hM (p i) (referenceQuery j) = 1 := by
  rw [referenceQuery, pointLoss_pair]
  norm_num [graphDist, firstDistance, unitDistance, hi, hij]

decl_89.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_center_reference
decl_89.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_center_reference
decl_89.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_89.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (j : Fin n),
  FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM (FTC.Counterexample.p j) (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) = 0
decl_89.source:
@[simp] theorem pointLoss_center_reference {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (j : Fin n) : pointLoss M hM (p j) (referenceQuery j) = 0 := by
  rw [referenceQuery, pointLoss_pair]
  rw [graphDist_self]
  simp only [zero_pow (by decide : (2 : ℕ) ≠ 0)]
  exact min_eq_right (sq_nonneg _)

/-- The corruption is assigned to `p_j` and contributes `M²`. -/

decl_87.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_b_reference
decl_87.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_b_reference
decl_87.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_87.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (j : Fin n),
  FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM FTC.Counterexample.b (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) = M ^ 2
decl_87.source:
@[simp] theorem pointLoss_b_reference {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (j : Fin n) : pointLoss M hM b (referenceQuery j) = M ^ 2 := by
  rw [referenceQuery, pointLoss_pair]
  change min ((M + 1 / 2) ^ 2) (M ^ 2) = M ^ 2
  apply min_eq_right
  nlinarith

decl_98.name: FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss_reference_le_one
decl_98.label: Counterexample.pointLoss_reference_le_one
decl_98.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_98.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (i j : Fin n),
  FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM (FTC.Counterexample.p i) (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) ≤ 1
decl_98.source:
theorem pointLoss_reference_le_one {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (i j : Fin n) : pointLoss M hM (p i) (referenceQuery j) ≤ 1 := by
  rw [referenceQuery, pointLoss_pair]
  calc
    min _ _ ≤ graphDist M (p i) (p j) ^ 2 := min_le_right _ _
    _ ≤ 1 := by
      by_cases hij : i = j <;> norm_num [graphDist, unitDistance, hij]

/-- Exact strict nearest-center assignment for the singleton. -/

decl_117.name: FTC.Counterexample.reference_first_nearest
decl_117.label: Counterexample.reference_first_nearest
decl_117.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_117.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (first j : Fin n),
  ↑first = 0 →
    ↑j ≠ 0 →
      FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M (FTC.Counterexample.p first) FTC.Counterexample.a <
        FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M (FTC.Counterexample.p first) (FTC.Counterexample.p j)
decl_117.source:
theorem reference_first_nearest {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (first j : Fin n)
    (hfirst : first.val = 0) (hj : j.val ≠ 0) :
    graphDist M (p first) a < graphDist M (p first) (p j) := by
  have hfj : first ≠ j := by
    intro h
    exact hj (h ▸ hfirst)
  norm_num [graphDist, firstDistance, unitDistance, hfirst, hfj]

/-- Every other original point is strictly closer to `p_j` than to `a`. -/

decl_119.name: FTC.Counterexample.reference_other_nearest
decl_119.label: Counterexample.reference_other_nearest
decl_119.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_119.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (i j : Fin n),
  ↑i ≠ 0 →
    FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M (FTC.Counterexample.p i) (FTC.Counterexample.p j) <
      FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M (FTC.Counterexample.p i) FTC.Counterexample.a
decl_119.source:
theorem reference_other_nearest {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (i j : Fin n)
    (hi : i.val ≠ 0) : graphDist M (p i) (p j) < graphDist M (p i) a := by
  have hle := unitDistance_le_one i j
  change unitDistance i j < firstDistance i
  rw [firstDistance, if_neg hi]
  linarith

/-- The corruption is strictly closer to `p_j` than to `a`. -/

decl_115.name: FTC.Counterexample.reference_b_nearest
decl_115.label: Counterexample.reference_b_nearest
decl_115.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_115.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (j : Fin n),
  FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M FTC.Counterexample.b (FTC.Counterexample.p j) <
    FTC.Counterexample.graphDist M FTC.Counterexample.b FTC.Counterexample.a
decl_115.source:
theorem reference_b_nearest {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (j : Fin n) :
    graphDist M b (p j) < graphDist (n := n) M b a := by
  change M < M + 1 / 2
  linarith

/-- A finite sum with two exceptional indices and a common value elsewhere. -/

decl_123.name: FTC.Counterexample.sum_two_specials
decl_123.label: Counterexample.sum_two_specials
decl_123.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_123.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → ℝ) (x y : Fin n),
  x ≠ y → ∀ (L : ℝ), (∀ (i : Fin n), i ≠ x → i ≠ y → f i = L) → ∑ i, f i = (↑n - 2) * L + f x + f y
decl_123.source:
theorem sum_two_specials {n : ℕ} (f : Fin n → ℝ) (x y : Fin n)
    (hxy : x ≠ y) (L : ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ i, i ≠ x → i ≠ y → f i = L) :
    (∑ i : Fin n, f i) = ((n : ℝ) - 2) * L + f x + f y := by
  let R : Finset (Fin n) := (Finset.univ.erase x).erase y
  have hy : y ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).erase x := by
    simp [Ne.symm hxy]
  have hcx := Finset.card_erase_add_one (Finset.mem_univ x)
  have hcy := Finset.card_erase_add_one hy
  have hcN : (R.card + 1) + 1 = n := by
    calc
      _ = (Finset.univ.erase x).card + 1 := congrArg (fun t : ℕ => t + 1) hcy
      _ = (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)).card := hcx
      _ = n := by simp
  have hcR' : ((R.card : ℝ) + 1) + 1 = (n : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hcN
  have hcR : (R.card : ℝ) = (n : ℝ) - 2 := by linarith
  have hRsum : (∑ i ∈ R, f i) = (R.card : ℝ) * L := by
    calc
      (∑ i ∈ R, f i) = ∑ _i ∈ R, L := by
        apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
        intro i hi
        exact hf i (Finset.mem_erase.mp (Finset.mem_erase.mp hi).2).1
          (Finset.mem_erase.mp hi).1
      _ = (R.card : ℝ) * L := by simp
  have hsx := Finset.sum_erase_add (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)) f (Finset.mem_univ x)
  have hsy := Finset.sum_erase_add (Finset.univ.erase x) f hy
  change (∑ i ∈ R, f i) + f y = ∑ i ∈ Finset.univ.erase x, f i at hsy
  calc
    (∑ i : Fin n, f i) = (∑ i ∈ R, f i) + f y + f x := by linarith
    _ = ((n : ℝ) - 2) * L + f x + f y := by rw [hRsum, hcR]; ring

decl_21.name: FTC.Counterexample.cleanCost_simplex
decl_21.label: Counterexample.cleanCost_simplex
decl_21.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_21.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l),
  FTC.Counterexample.cleanCost M hM (FTC.Counterexample.simplexQuery j l hjl) = ↑n - 2
decl_21.source:
@[simp] theorem cleanCost_simplex {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l) :
    cleanCost M hM (simplexQuery j l hjl) = (n : ℝ) - 2 := by
  have hs := sum_two_specials
    (fun i => pointLoss M hM (p i) (simplexQuery j l hjl)) j l hjl 1
    (fun i hij hil => by rw [pointLoss_simplex, if_neg hij, if_neg hil])
  simp only [cleanCost, FTC.cost, cleanContribution_apply]
  simpa only [pointLoss_simplex, if_pos rfl, if_neg (Ne.symm hjl), ite_true,
    mul_one, add_zero] using hs

/-- Replacing one unit-weight entry changes every query cost by subtracting
its original loss and adding its new loss. -/

decl_39.name: FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost_eq_cleanCost_sub_add
decl_39.label: Counterexample.corruptCost_eq_cleanCost_sub_add
decl_39.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_39.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (bad : Fin n) (S : FTC.Counterexample.Query n),
  FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost M hM bad S =
    FTC.Counterexample.cleanCost M hM S - FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM (FTC.Counterexample.p bad) S +
      FTC.Counterexample.pointLoss M hM FTC.Counterexample.b S
decl_39.source:
theorem corruptCost_eq_cleanCost_sub_add {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad : Fin n) (S : Query n) :
    corruptCost M hM bad S = cleanCost M hM S -
      pointLoss M hM (p bad) S + pointLoss M hM b S := by
  have hc := FTC.cost_erase_add (cleanContribution M hM)
    (Q := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n))) (i := bad) (Finset.mem_univ bad) S
  have hb := FTC.cost_erase_add (corruptContribution M hM bad)
    (Q := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n))) (i := bad) (Finset.mem_univ bad) S
  have he : FTC.cost (corruptContribution M hM bad) (Finset.univ.erase bad) S =
      FTC.cost (cleanContribution M hM) (Finset.univ.erase bad) S := by
    apply FTC.cost_congr
    intro i hi T
    simp only [corruptContribution_apply, if_neg (Finset.mem_erase.mp hi).1,
      cleanContribution_apply]
  change FTC.cost (cleanContribution M hM) (Finset.univ.erase bad) S +
    cleanContribution M hM bad S = cleanCost M hM S at hc
  change FTC.cost (corruptContribution M hM bad) (Finset.univ.erase bad) S +
    corruptContribution M hM bad bad S = corruptCost M hM bad S at hb
  simp only [corruptContribution_apply, ite_true] at hb
  simp only [cleanContribution_apply] at hc
  rw [he] at hb
  linarith

/-- The witness query has corrupted cost `n-3+M²`. -/

decl_41.name: FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost_simplex
decl_41.label: Counterexample.corruptCost_simplex
decl_41.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_41.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (bad j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l),
  bad ≠ j → bad ≠ l → FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost M hM bad (FTC.Counterexample.simplexQuery j l hjl) = ↑n - 3 + M ^ 2
decl_41.source:
theorem corruptCost_simplex {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l) (hbj : bad ≠ j) (hbl : bad ≠ l) :
    corruptCost M hM bad (simplexQuery j l hjl) = (n : ℝ) - 3 + M ^ 2 := by
  rw [corruptCost_eq_cleanCost_sub_add, cleanCost_simplex, pointLoss_b_simplex,
    pointLoss_simplex, if_neg hbj, if_neg hbl]
  ring

/-- Filtering out the genuine singleton leaves cost `n-4+M²` on the witness
query, since it also had unit loss there. -/

decl_50.name: FTC.Counterexample.cost_erase_first_simplex
decl_50.label: Counterexample.cost_erase_first_simplex
decl_50.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_50.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (bad first j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l),
  bad ≠ j →
    bad ≠ l →
      first ≠ bad →
        first ≠ j →
          first ≠ l →
            FTC.cost (FTC.Counterexample.corruptContribution M hM bad) (Finset.univ.erase first)
                (FTC.Counterexample.simplexQuery j l hjl) =
              ↑n - 4 + M ^ 2
decl_50.source:
theorem cost_erase_first_simplex {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad first j l : Fin n) (hjl : j ≠ l)
    (hbj : bad ≠ j) (hbl : bad ≠ l) (hfb : first ≠ bad)
    (hfj : first ≠ j) (hfl : first ≠ l) :
    FTC.cost (corruptContribution M hM bad) (Finset.univ.erase first)
      (simplexQuery j l hjl) = (n : ℝ) - 4 + M ^ 2 := by
  have he := FTC.cost_erase_add (corruptContribution M hM bad)
    (Q := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n))) (i := first) (Finset.mem_univ first)
    (simplexQuery j l hjl)
  have hf : corruptContribution M hM bad first (simplexQuery j l hjl) = 1 := by
    simp only [corruptContribution_apply, if_neg hfb, pointLoss_simplex,
      if_neg hfj, if_neg hfl]
  change FTC.cost (corruptContribution M hM bad) (Finset.univ.erase first)
      (simplexQuery j l hjl) + corruptContribution M hM bad first (simplexQuery j l hjl) =
    corruptCost M hM bad (simplexQuery j l hjl) at he
  rw [hf, corruptCost_simplex M hM bad j l hjl hbj hbl] at he
  linarith

decl_20.name: FTC.Counterexample.cleanCost_reference
decl_20.label: Counterexample.cleanCost_reference
decl_20.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_20.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (first j : Fin n),
  ↑first = 0 → ↑j ≠ 0 → FTC.Counterexample.cleanCost M hM (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) = ↑n - 2 + 1 / 4
decl_20.source:
theorem cleanCost_reference {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (first j : Fin n) (hfirst : first.val = 0) (hj : j.val ≠ 0) :
    cleanCost M hM (referenceQuery j) = (n : ℝ) - 2 + 1 / 4 := by
  have hfj : first ≠ j := by intro h; exact hj (h ▸ hfirst)
  have hs := sum_two_specials (fun i => pointLoss M hM (p i) (referenceQuery j))
    first j hfj 1 (by
      intro i hif hij
      have hi : i.val ≠ 0 := by
        intro hi0
        apply hif
        apply Fin.ext
        exact hi0.trans hfirst.symm
      exact pointLoss_other_reference M hM i j hi hij)
  simp only [cleanCost, FTC.cost, cleanContribution_apply]
  simpa only [pointLoss_first_reference M hM first j hfirst hj,
    pointLoss_center_reference, mul_one, add_zero] using hs

/-- The reference clustering has exactly the cost stated in Appendix A.1. -/

decl_40.name: FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost_reference
decl_40.label: Counterexample.corruptCost_reference
decl_40.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Counterexample/Witnesses.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_40.statement:
∀ {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M) (bad first j : Fin n),
  ↑first = 0 →
    ↑j ≠ 0 →
      ↑bad ≠ 0 →
        bad ≠ j → FTC.Counterexample.corruptCost M hM bad (FTC.Counterexample.referenceQuery j) = ↑n - 3 + 1 / 4 + M ^ 2
decl_40.source:
theorem corruptCost_reference {n : ℕ} (M : ℝ) (hM : 1 ≤ M)
    (bad first j : Fin n) (hfirst : first.val = 0)
    (hj : j.val ≠ 0) (hbad : bad.val ≠ 0) (hbj : bad ≠ j) :
    corruptCost M hM bad (referenceQuery j) =
      (n : ℝ) - 3 + 1 / 4 + M ^ 2 := by
  rw [corruptCost_eq_cleanCost_sub_add, cleanCost_reference M hM first j hfirst hj,
    pointLoss_other_reference M hM bad j hbad hbj, pointLoss_b_reference]
  ring

end

end FTC.Counterexample

decl_139.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.referenceCost
decl_139.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.referenceCost
decl_139.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_139.source:
def referenceCost (n : ℝ) : ℝ := 2 * n - 27 / 4

/-- Proxy score of the genuine singleton `p₁`. -/

decl_142.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.singletonProxy
decl_142.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.singletonProxy
decl_142.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_142.source:
def singletonProxy (n : ℝ) : ℝ := 2 + 1 / (2 * referenceCost n)

/-- Proxy score of the corruption `b`. -/

decl_127.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionProxy
decl_127.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionProxy
decl_127.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_127.source:
def corruptionProxy (n : ℝ) : ℝ := 2 / (n - 1) + 2 * (n - 4) / referenceCost n

/-- Upper bound on proxy scores of the other genuine entries. -/

decl_136.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.ordinaryProxy
decl_136.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.ordinaryProxy
decl_136.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_136.source:
def ordinaryProxy (n : ℝ) : ℝ := 2 / (n - 1) + 2 / referenceCost n

/-- The paper's uniform upper bound on genuine-entry sensitivities. -/

decl_132.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.genuineBound
decl_132.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.genuineBound
decl_132.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_132.source:
def genuineBound (n : ℝ) : ℝ := 1 / (n - 3)

/-- The sensitivity ratio of `b` witnessed by `{p₂,p₃}`. -/

decl_130.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionWitness
decl_130.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionWitness
decl_130.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_130.source:
def corruptionWitness (n : ℝ) : ℝ := (n - 4) / (2 * n - 7)

/-- Distortion after the proxy rule removes `p₁` and retains `b`. -/

decl_145.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.wrongDistortion
decl_145.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.wrongDistortion
decl_145.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.

decl_140.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.referenceCost_pos
decl_140.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.referenceCost_pos
decl_140.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_140.source:
theorem referenceCost_pos {n : ℝ} (hn : 8 ≤ n) : 0 < referenceCost n := by
  unfold referenceCost
  linarith

decl_143.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.singletonProxy_gt_two
decl_143.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.singletonProxy_gt_two
decl_143.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_143.source:
theorem singletonProxy_gt_two {n : ℝ} (hn : 8 ≤ n) : 2 < singletonProxy n := by
  have hd := referenceCost_pos hn
  have hp : 0 < 1 / (2 * referenceCost n) :=
    one_div_pos.mpr (by linarith)
  unfold singletonProxy
  linarith

decl_128.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionProxy_gt_one
decl_128.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionProxy_gt_one
decl_128.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_128.source:
theorem corruptionProxy_gt_one {n : ℝ} (hn : 8 ≤ n) : 1 < corruptionProxy n := by
  have hd := referenceCost_pos hn
  have hn1 : 0 < n - 1 := by linarith
  unfold corruptionProxy
  rw [div_add_div _ _ (ne_of_gt hn1) (ne_of_gt hd)]
  apply (lt_div_iff₀ (mul_pos hn1 hd)).2
  unfold referenceCost
  nlinarith

decl_129.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionProxy_lt_two
decl_129.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionProxy_lt_two
decl_129.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_129.source:
theorem corruptionProxy_lt_two {n : ℝ} (hn : 8 ≤ n) : corruptionProxy n < 2 := by
  have hd := referenceCost_pos hn
  have hfirst : 2 / (n - 1) < 1 :=
    (div_lt_one (by linarith)).2 (by linarith)
  have hsecond : 2 * (n - 4) / referenceCost n < 1 := by
    apply (div_lt_one hd).2
    unfold referenceCost
    linarith
  unfold corruptionProxy
  linarith

decl_137.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.ordinaryProxy_lt_two
decl_137.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.ordinaryProxy_lt_two
decl_137.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_137.source:
theorem ordinaryProxy_lt_two {n : ℝ} (hn : 8 ≤ n) : ordinaryProxy n < 2 := by
  have hd := referenceCost_pos hn
  have hfirst : 2 / (n - 1) < 1 :=
    (div_lt_one (by linarith)).2 (by linarith)
  have hsecond : 2 / referenceCost n < 1 := by
    apply (div_lt_one hd).2
    unfold referenceCost
    linarith
  unfold ordinaryProxy
  linarith

/-- The claimed genuine-sensitivity bound lies below the cluster-size term
of every nonsingleton proxy. -/

decl_133.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.genuineBound_le_cluster_term
decl_133.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.genuineBound_le_cluster_term
decl_133.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_133.source:
theorem genuineBound_le_cluster_term {n : ℝ} (hn : 8 ≤ n) :
    genuineBound n ≤ 2 / (n - 1) := by
  unfold genuineBound
  apply (div_le_div_iff₀ (by linarith : 0 < n - 3) (by linarith : 0 < n - 1)).2
  linarith

/-- The witnessed corruption sensitivity strictly exceeds the bound for all
of the genuine entries. -/

decl_134.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.genuineBound_lt_corruptionWitness
decl_134.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.genuineBound_lt_corruptionWitness
decl_134.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_134.source:
theorem genuineBound_lt_corruptionWitness {n : ℝ} (hn : 8 ≤ n) :
    genuineBound n < corruptionWitness n := by
  unfold genuineBound corruptionWitness
  apply (div_lt_div_iff₀ (by linarith : 0 < n - 3)
    (by linarith : 0 < 2 * n - 7)).2
  have hp := mul_nonneg (by linarith : 0 ≤ n - 8) (by linarith : 0 ≤ n - 1)
  nlinarith

/-- Given the paper's lower bound `n-3` on optimum cost, its reference
clustering satisfies the asserted factor-two guarantee. -/

decl_141.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.reference_two_approx
decl_141.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.reference_two_approx
decl_141.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_141.statement: ∀ {n opt : ℝ}, n - 3 ≤ opt → FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.referenceCost n ≤ 2 * opt
decl_141.source:
theorem reference_two_approx {n opt : ℝ} (hopt : n - 3 ≤ opt) :
    referenceCost n ≤ 2 * opt := by
  unfold referenceCost
  linarith

/-- All strict scalar separations needed for the opposite proxy/exact choices. -/

decl_138.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.proxy_and_sensitivity_separations
decl_138.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.proxy_and_sensitivity_separations
decl_138.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_138.statement:
∀ {n : ℝ},
  8 ≤ n →
    2 < FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.singletonProxy n ∧
      1 < FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionProxy n ∧
        FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionProxy n < 2 ∧
          FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.ordinaryProxy n < 2 ∧
            FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.genuineBound n ≤ 2 / (n - 1) ∧
              FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.genuineBound n < FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionWitness n
decl_138.source:
theorem proxy_and_sensitivity_separations {n : ℝ} (hn : 8 ≤ n) :
    2 < singletonProxy n ∧
    1 < corruptionProxy n ∧ corruptionProxy n < 2 ∧
    ordinaryProxy n < 2 ∧ genuineBound n ≤ 2 / (n - 1) ∧
    genuineBound n < corruptionWitness n := by
  exact ⟨singletonProxy_gt_two hn, corruptionProxy_gt_one hn,
    corruptionProxy_lt_two hn, ordinaryProxy_lt_two hn,
    genuineBound_le_cluster_term hn, genuineBound_lt_corruptionWitness hn⟩

/-- The parameter regime of the PDF implies all the numerical size
conditions used above. -/

decl_144.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.size_ge_eight
decl_144.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.size_ge_eight
decl_144.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_144.source:
theorem size_ge_eight {ε n : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) (hεsmall : ε < 1 / 10)
    (hn : 8 / ε ≤ n) : 8 ≤ n := by
  have h : 8 ≤ 8 / ε := (le_div_iff₀ hε).2 (by linarith)
  exact h.trans hn

/-- Exact distortion and clean-deletion error estimates from Appendix A.1. -/

decl_131.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.distortion_and_deletion_bounds
decl_131.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.distortion_and_deletion_bounds
decl_131.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_131.statement:
∀ {ε n : ℝ},
  0 < ε →
    ε < 1 / 10 →
      8 / ε ≤ n → 2 - ε ≤ FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.wrongDistortion n ∧ 1 + 6 * ε < 2 - ε ∧ 1 / (n - 2) ≤ ε
decl_131.source:
theorem distortion_and_deletion_bounds {ε n : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hεsmall : ε < 1 / 10) (hn : 8 / ε ≤ n) :
    2 - ε ≤ wrongDistortion n ∧ 1 + 6 * ε < 2 - ε ∧
    1 / (n - 2) ≤ ε := by
  have hn8 := size_ge_eight hε hεsmall hn
  have hn2 : 0 < n - 2 := by linarith
  have hbudget : 8 ≤ n * ε := (div_le_iff₀ hε).1 hn
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · unfold wrongDistortion
    apply (le_div_iff₀ hn2).2
    nlinarith
  · linarith
  · apply (div_le_iff₀ hn2).2
    nlinarith

/-- The scalar distortion formula exceeds the upper coreset tolerance. -/

decl_146.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.wrongDistortion_gt_tolerance
decl_146.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.wrongDistortion_gt_tolerance
decl_146.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_146.statement: ∀ {ε n : ℝ}, 0 < ε → ε < 1 / 10 → 8 / ε ≤ n → 1 + 6 * ε < FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.wrongDistortion n
decl_146.source:
theorem wrongDistortion_gt_tolerance {ε n : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hεsmall : ε < 1 / 10) (hn : 8 / ε ≤ n) :
    1 + 6 * ε < wrongDistortion n := by
  obtain ⟨hlarge, hgap, _⟩ := distortion_and_deletion_bounds hε hεsmall hn
  exact hgap.trans_le hlarge

/-- An elementary selection consequence: if the scalar bounds for the
metric construction hold uniformly over its entries, the two score rules have
different strict maximizers. The metric hypotheses themselves are not proved
in this file. -/

decl_135.name: FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.opposite_strict_maximizers
decl_135.label: CounterexampleArithmetic.opposite_strict_maximizers
decl_135.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/CounterexampleArithmetic.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_135.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [DecidableEq I] (Q : Finset I) (g b : I) (proxy exactScore : I → ℝ) {n : ℝ},
  8 ≤ n →
    g ∈ Q →
      b ∈ Q →
        g ≠ b →
          proxy g = FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.singletonProxy n →
            (∀ i ∈ Q, i ≠ g → proxy i ≤ 2) →
              FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.corruptionWitness n ≤ exactScore b →
                (∀ i ∈ Q, i ≠ b → exactScore i ≤ FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic.genuineBound n) →
                  (g ∈ Q ∧ ∀ i ∈ Q, i ≠ g → proxy i < proxy g) ∧
                    (b ∈ Q ∧ ∀ i ∈ Q, i ≠ b → exactScore i < exactScore b) ∧ g ≠ b
decl_135.source:
theorem opposite_strict_maximizers {I : Type*} [DecidableEq I]
    (Q : Finset I) (g b : I) (proxy exactScore : I → ℝ) {n : ℝ}
    (hn : 8 ≤ n) (hg : g ∈ Q) (hb : b ∈ Q) (hgb : g ≠ b)
    (hproxy : proxy g = singletonProxy n)
    (hotherProxy : ∀ i ∈ Q, i ≠ g → proxy i ≤ 2)
    (hexactBad : corruptionWitness n ≤ exactScore b)
    (hexactGood : ∀ i ∈ Q, i ≠ b → exactScore i ≤ genuineBound n) :
    (g ∈ Q ∧ ∀ i ∈ Q, i ≠ g → proxy i < proxy g) ∧
    (b ∈ Q ∧ ∀ i ∈ Q, i ≠ b → exactScore i < exactScore b) ∧ g ≠ b := by
  refine ⟨⟨hg, ?_⟩, ⟨hb, ?_⟩, hgb⟩
  · intro i hi hig
    rw [hproxy]
    exact (hotherProxy i hi hig).trans_lt (singletonProxy_gt_two hn)
  · intro i hi hib
    exact (hexactGood i hi hib).trans_lt
      ((genuineBound_lt_corruptionWitness hn).trans_le hexactBad)

end

end FTC.CounterexampleArithmetic

decl_652.name: FTC.clean_core_bounds
decl_652.label: Clean-core invariant
decl_652.summary: Bounds the clean part of a corrupted summary throughout filtering.
decl_652.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq I] {c d : I → S → ℝ} {reference : S → ℝ} {U B Q : Finset I} {f : ℕ}
  {ε δ : ℝ},
  (∀ (i : I) (s : S), 0 ≤ c i s) →
    (∀ (s : S), 0 ≤ reference s) →
      FTC.IsCoreset ε reference (FTC.cost c U) →
        (∀ i ∈ U, i ∉ B → ∀ (s : S), d i s = c i s) →
          (∀ i ∈ U, ∀ (s : S), c i s ≤ δ * reference s) →
            Q ⊆ U →
              B.card ≤ f →
                (U \ Q).card ≤ f →
                  0 ≤ δ →
                    ↑f * δ ≤ ε →
                      ∀ (s : S),
                        (1 - 3 * ε) * reference s ≤ FTC.cost d (Q \ B) s ∧ FTC.cost d (Q \ B) s ≤ (1 + ε) * reference s
decl_652.source:
theorem clean_core_bounds {c d : I → S → ℝ} {reference : S → ℝ}
    {U B Q : Finset I} {f : ℕ} {ε δ : ℝ}
    (hc : ∀ i s, 0 ≤ c i s) (hreference : ∀ s, 0 ≤ reference s)
    (hcoreset : IsCoreset ε reference (cost c U))
    (hagrees : ∀ i ∈ U, i ∉ B → ∀ s, d i s = c i s)
    (hentry : ∀ i ∈ U, ∀ s, c i s ≤ δ * reference s)
    (hQ : Q ⊆ U) (hB : B.card ≤ f) (hlost : (U \ Q).card ≤ f)
    (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hbudget : (f : ℝ) * δ ≤ ε) :
    ∀ s, (1 - 3 * ε) * reference s ≤ cost d (Q \ B) s ∧
      cost d (Q \ B) s ≤ (1 + ε) * reference s := by
  intro s
  let A := Q \ B
  have hAU : A ⊆ U := (Finset.sdiff_subset : Q \ B ⊆ Q).trans hQ
  have heq : cost d A s = cost c A s := by
    apply cost_congr
    intro i hi t
    have hiQ := (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hi).1
    exact hagrees i (hQ hiQ) (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hi).2 t
  have hcompl : U \ A ⊆ B ∪ (U \ Q) := by
    intro i hi
    obtain ⟨hiU, hiA⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hi
    by_cases hiB : i ∈ B
    · exact Finset.mem_union_left _ hiB
    · apply Finset.mem_union_right
      apply Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr
      refine ⟨hiU, ?_⟩
      intro hiQ
      exact hiA (Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hiQ, hiB⟩)
  have hcard : (U \ A).card ≤ 2 * f := by
    have h1 := Finset.card_le_card hcompl
    have h2 := Finset.card_union_le B (U \ Q)
    omega
  have hcardR : ((U \ A).card : ℝ) ≤ 2 * (f : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast hcard
  have hloss : cost c (U \ A) s ≤ 2 * ε * reference s := by
    calc
      cost c (U \ A) s ≤ ((U \ A).card : ℝ) * (δ * reference s) :=
        cost_le_card_mul (fun i hi => hentry i (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hi).1 s)
      _ ≤ (2 * (f : ℝ)) * (δ * reference s) :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hcardR (mul_nonneg hδ (hreference s))
      _ = 2 * ((f : ℝ) * δ) * reference s := by ring
      _ ≤ 2 * ε * reference s :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right
          (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hbudget (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)) (hreference s)
  have hdecomp := cost_sdiff_add c hAU s
  have hmono := cost_mono hc hAU s
  have hco := hcoreset s
  change (1 - 3 * ε) * reference s ≤ cost d A s ∧
    cost d A s ≤ (1 + ε) * reference s
  rw [heq]
  constructor <;> linarith

/-- Main deterministic filtering theorem, with the actual iterative decoder.
It includes the empty-summary and zero-fault cases. -/

decl_676.name: FTC.filtering_decoder_correct_with_rule
decl_676.label: filtering_decoder_correct_with_rule
decl_676.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Decoder.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_676.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq I] {c d : I → S → ℝ} {reference : S → ℝ} {U B : Finset I} {f : ℕ}
  {ε δ α : ℝ},
  (∀ (i : I) (s : S), 0 ≤ c i s) →
    (∀ (i : I) (s : S), 0 ≤ d i s) →
      (∀ (s : S), 0 ≤ reference s) →
        0 ≤ ε →
          ε < 1 / 10 →
            0 ≤ δ →
              1 ≤ α →
                FTC.IsCoreset ε reference (FTC.cost c U) →
                  B.card ≤ f →
                    (∀ i ∈ U, i ∉ B → ∀ (s : S), d i s = c i s) →
                      (∀ i ∈ U, ∀ (s : S), c i s ≤ δ * reference s) →
                        ↑f * α * δ ≤ ε →
                          ∀ (oracle : FTC.ApproxSensitivityOracle d α) (rule : FTC.SelectionRule I),
                            rule.IsMaxFor oracle.score →
                              FTC.IsCoreset (6 * ε) reference (FTC.cost d (FTC.selectionRun rule f U))
decl_676.source:
theorem filtering_decoder_correct_with_rule {c d : I → S → ℝ} {reference : S → ℝ}
    {U B : Finset I} {f : ℕ} {ε δ α : ℝ}
    (hc : ∀ i s, 0 ≤ c i s) (hd : ∀ i s, 0 ≤ d i s)
    (hreference : ∀ s, 0 ≤ reference s)
    (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hεsmall : ε < 1 / 10) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hα : 1 ≤ α)
    (hcoreset : IsCoreset ε reference (cost c U))
    (hB : B.card ≤ f)
    (hagrees : ∀ i ∈ U, i ∉ B → ∀ s, d i s = c i s)
    (hentry : ∀ i ∈ U, ∀ s, c i s ≤ δ * reference s)
    (hbudget : (f : ℝ) * α * δ ≤ ε)
    (oracle : ApproxSensitivityOracle d α)
    (rule : SelectionRule I) (hmaximum : rule.IsMaxFor oracle.score) :
    IsCoreset (6 * ε) reference (cost d (selectionRun rule f U)) := by
  have hα0 : 0 ≤ α := by linarith
  have hf : 0 ≤ (f : ℝ) := Nat.cast_nonneg f
  have hfd : (f : ℝ) * δ ≤ ε := by
    calc
      (f : ℝ) * δ = ((f : ℝ) * δ) * 1 := by ring
      _ ≤ ((f : ℝ) * δ) * α :=
        mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hα (mul_nonneg hf hδ)
      _ = (f : ℝ) * α * δ := by ring
      _ ≤ ε := hbudget
  let R := selectionRun rule f U
  have hR : R ⊆ U := selectionRun_subset rule f U
  have hcleanR := clean_core_bounds hc hreference hcoreset hagrees hentry hR hB
    (selection_removed_card_le rule f U) hδ hfd
  have hlower : ∀ s, (1 - 6 * ε) * reference s ≤ cost d R s := by
    intro s
    have hmono := cost_mono hd (Finset.sdiff_subset : R \ B ⊆ R) s
    have hlow := (hcleanR s).1
    have hnonneg := hreference s
    nlinarith
  by_cases hbad : (R ∩ B).Nonempty
  · obtain ⟨t, ht, g, hg, hgB, hmax⟩ :=
      selection_good_stage_of_bad_remaining rule hmaximum U B f hB hbad
    let Q := selectionRun rule t U
    have hQ : Q ⊆ U := selectionRun_subset rule t U
    have hRQ : R ⊆ Q := selectionRun_antitone rule ht.le U
    have hcleanQ := clean_core_bounds hc hreference hcoreset hagrees hentry hQ hB
      ((selection_removed_card_le rule t U).trans ht.le) hδ hfd
    have hgood : sensitivity d Q g ≤ 2 * δ := by
      apply sensitivity_le_of_contribution_le hd hg (by positivity)
      intro s
      have hsmall : d g s ≤ δ * reference s := by
        rw [hagrees g (hQ hg) hgB s]
        exact hentry g (hQ hg) s
      have hmono := cost_mono hd (Finset.sdiff_subset : Q \ B ⊆ Q) s
      have hlow := (hcleanQ s).1
      have hhalf : (1 / 2 : ℝ) * reference s ≤ cost d Q s := by
        have hcoef : (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ 1 - 3 * ε := by linarith
        have := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hcoef (hreference s)
        linarith
      have hscale := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hhalf hδ
      nlinarith
    have hbadSensitivity : ∀ b ∈ Q, sensitivity d Q b ≤ α * (2 * δ) := by
      intro b hb
      calc
        sensitivity d Q b ≤ α * oracle.score Q b := oracle.lower Q b hb
        _ ≤ α * oracle.score Q g := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hmax b hb) hα0
        _ ≤ α * sensitivity d Q g :=
          mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (oracle.upper Q g hg) hα0
        _ ≤ α * (2 * δ) := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hgood hα0
    have hupperQ : ∀ s, cost d Q s ≤ (1 + 6 * ε) * reference s := by
      intro s
      have hcost0 := cost_nonneg hd Q s
      have hbadpart : cost d (Q ∩ B) s ≤ 2 * ε * cost d Q s := by
        have hcard : ((Q ∩ B).card : ℝ) ≤ (f : ℝ) := by
          exact_mod_cast (Finset.card_le_card (Finset.inter_subset_right : Q ∩ B ⊆ B)).trans hB
        calc
          cost d (Q ∩ B) s ≤ ((Q ∩ B).card : ℝ) * ((α * (2 * δ)) * cost d Q s) := by
            apply cost_le_card_mul
            intro b hb
            have hbQ := (Finset.mem_inter.mp hb).1
            exact (contribution_le_sensitivity_mul_cost hd hbQ s).trans
              (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (hbadSensitivity b hbQ) hcost0)
          _ ≤ (f : ℝ) * ((α * (2 * δ)) * cost d Q s) :=
            mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hcard (by positivity)
          _ = (2 * ((f : ℝ) * α * δ)) * cost d Q s := by ring
          _ ≤ 2 * ε * cost d Q s :=
            mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right
              (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hbudget (by norm_num : (0 : ℝ) ≤ 2)) hcost0
      have hdecomp := cost_sdiff_add_inter d Q B s
      have hcleanupper := (hcleanQ s).2
      have htotal : (1 - 2 * ε) * cost d Q s ≤ (1 + ε) * reference s := by
        nlinarith
      have hcoef : 1 + ε ≤ (1 - 2 * ε) * (1 + 6 * ε) := by
        have : 0 ≤ ε * (1 - 4 * ε) := mul_nonneg hε (by linarith)
        nlinarith
      have hscale := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right hcoef (hreference s)
      have hden : 0 < 1 - 2 * ε := by linarith
      have hscaled : (1 - 2 * ε) * cost d Q s ≤
          (1 - 2 * ε) * ((1 + 6 * ε) * reference s) := by
        calc
          (1 - 2 * ε) * cost d Q s ≤ (1 + ε) * reference s := htotal
          _ ≤ (1 - 2 * ε) * ((1 + 6 * ε) * reference s) := by nlinarith [hscale]
      exact le_of_mul_le_mul_left hscaled hden
    intro s
    exact ⟨hlower s, (cost_mono hd hRQ s).trans (hupperQ s)⟩
  · have hbadEmpty : R ∩ B = ∅ := Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.mp hbad
    intro s
    refine ⟨hlower s, ?_⟩
    have hdecomp := cost_sdiff_add_inter d R B s
    have hcleanupper := (hcleanR s).2
    have hzero : cost d (R ∩ B) s = 0 := by simp [hbadEmpty]
    have hnonneg := hreference s
    nlinarith


/-- The original real-score decoder is a specialization of the selection-rule theorem. -/

decl_674.name: FTC.filtering_decoder_correct
decl_674.label: Filtering decoder correctness
decl_674.summary: Proves the iterative filtering decoder returns a 6ε-coreset under the stated corruption and oracle hypotheses.
decl_674.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq I] {c d : I → S → ℝ} {reference : S → ℝ} {U B : Finset I} {f : ℕ}
  {ε δ α : ℝ},
  (∀ (i : I) (s : S), 0 ≤ c i s) →
    (∀ (i : I) (s : S), 0 ≤ d i s) →
      (∀ (s : S), 0 ≤ reference s) →
        0 ≤ ε →
          ε < 1 / 10 →
            0 ≤ δ →
              1 ≤ α →
                FTC.IsCoreset ε reference (FTC.cost c U) →
                  B.card ≤ f →
                    (∀ i ∈ U, i ∉ B → ∀ (s : S), d i s = c i s) →
                      (∀ i ∈ U, ∀ (s : S), c i s ≤ δ * reference s) →
                        ↑f * α * δ ≤ ε →
                          ∀ (oracle : FTC.ApproxSensitivityOracle d α),
                            FTC.IsCoreset (6 * ε) reference (FTC.cost d (FTC.peel oracle.score f U))
decl_674.source:
theorem filtering_decoder_correct {c d : I → S → ℝ} {reference : S → ℝ}
    {U B : Finset I} {f : ℕ} {ε δ α : ℝ}
    (hc : ∀ i s, 0 ≤ c i s) (hd : ∀ i s, 0 ≤ d i s)
    (hreference : ∀ s, 0 ≤ reference s)
    (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hεsmall : ε < 1 / 10) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hα : 1 ≤ α)
    (hcoreset : IsCoreset ε reference (cost c U))
    (hB : B.card ≤ f)
    (hagrees : ∀ i ∈ U, i ∉ B → ∀ s, d i s = c i s)
    (hentry : ∀ i ∈ U, ∀ s, c i s ≤ δ * reference s)
    (hbudget : (f : ℝ) * α * δ ≤ ε)
    (oracle : ApproxSensitivityOracle d α) :
    IsCoreset (6 * ε) reference (cost d (peel oracle.score f U)) := by
  rw [peel_eq_selectionRun]
  exact filtering_decoder_correct_with_rule hc hd hreference hε hεsmall hδ hα
    hcoreset hB hagrees hentry hbudget oracle (classicalSelectionRule oracle.score)
    (classicalSelectionRule_isMaxFor oracle.score)

/-- Entry-level form: the decoder only uses the corrupted summary and the
approximate-sensitivity oracle for that summary. -/

decl_675.name: FTC.filtering_decoder_correct_of_corruption
decl_675.label: filtering_decoder_correct_of_corruption
decl_675.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Decoder.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_675.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} {X : Type u_3} [inst : DecidableEq I] (loss : X → S → ℝ),
  (∀ (x : X) (s : S), 0 ≤ loss x s) →
    ∀ (reference : S → ℝ),
      (∀ (s : S), 0 ≤ reference s) →
        ∀ (U : Finset I) (entries corrupted : I → FTC.Entry X) {f : ℕ} {ε δ α : ℝ},
          0 ≤ ε →
            ε < 1 / 10 →
              0 ≤ δ →
                1 ≤ α →
                  FTC.IsCoreset ε reference (FTC.cost (FTC.contribution loss entries) U) →
                    FTC.IsFCorruption f U entries corrupted →
                      (∀ i ∈ U, ∀ (s : S), FTC.contribution loss entries i s ≤ δ * reference s) →
                        ↑f * α * δ ≤ ε →
                          ∀ (oracle : FTC.ApproxSensitivityOracle (FTC.contribution loss corrupted) α),
                            FTC.IsCoreset (6 * ε) reference
                              (FTC.cost (FTC.contribution loss corrupted) (FTC.peel oracle.score f U))
decl_675.source:
theorem filtering_decoder_correct_of_corruption
    (loss : X → S → ℝ) (hloss : ∀ x s, 0 ≤ loss x s)
    (reference : S → ℝ) (hreference : ∀ s, 0 ≤ reference s)
    (U : Finset I) (entries corrupted : I → Entry X) {f : ℕ} {ε δ α : ℝ}
    (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hεsmall : ε < 1 / 10) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ) (hα : 1 ≤ α)
    (hcoreset : IsCoreset ε reference (cost (contribution loss entries) U))
    (hcorrupt : IsFCorruption f U entries corrupted)
    (hentry : ∀ i ∈ U, ∀ s, contribution loss entries i s ≤ δ * reference s)
    (hbudget : (f : ℝ) * α * δ ≤ ε)
    (oracle : ApproxSensitivityOracle (contribution loss corrupted) α) :
    IsCoreset (6 * ε) reference
      (cost (contribution loss corrupted) (peel oracle.score f U)) := by
  obtain ⟨B, _, hB, hagrees⟩ := hcorrupt
  apply filtering_decoder_correct
    (contribution_nonneg loss entries hloss) (contribution_nonneg loss corrupted hloss)
    hreference hε hεsmall hδ hα hcoreset hB ?_ hentry hbudget oracle
  intro i hi hiB s
  simp only [contribution, hagrees i hi hiB]

end FTC

decl_199.name: FTC.Executable.matrixDecode_correct
decl_199.label: Executable.matrixDecode_correct
decl_199.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Decoder.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_199.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : LinearOrder I] [DecidableEq S] {a c : I → S → ℚ} {reference : S → ℝ}
  {queries : Finset S} {U B : Finset I} {f : ℕ} {ε δ : ℝ},
  (∀ (i : I) (s : S), 0 ≤ a i s) →
    (∀ (i : I) (s : S), 0 ≤ c i s) →
      (∀ (s : S), s ∈ queries) →
        (∀ (s : S), 0 ≤ reference s) →
          0 ≤ ε →
            ε < 1 / 10 →
              0 ≤ δ →
                FTC.IsCoreset ε reference (FTC.cost (FTC.Executable.realContribution a) U) →
                  B.card ≤ f →
                    (∀ i ∈ U, i ∉ B → ∀ (s : S), c i s = a i s) →
                      (∀ i ∈ U, ∀ (s : S), FTC.Executable.realContribution a i s ≤ δ * reference s) →
                        ↑f * δ ≤ ε →
                          FTC.IsCoreset (6 * ε) reference
                            (FTC.cost (FTC.Executable.realContribution c) (FTC.Executable.matrixDecode c queries f U))
decl_199.source:
theorem matrixDecode_correct {a c : I → S → ℚ} {reference : S → ℝ}
    {queries : Finset S} {U B : Finset I} {f : ℕ} {ε δ : ℝ}
    (ha : ∀ i s, 0 ≤ a i s) (hc : ∀ i s, 0 ≤ c i s)
    (hqueries : ∀ s : S, s ∈ queries) (hreference : ∀ s, 0 ≤ reference s)
    (hε : 0 ≤ ε) (hεsmall : ε < 1 / 10) (hδ : 0 ≤ δ)
    (hcoreset : IsCoreset ε reference (cost (realContribution a) U))
    (hB : B.card ≤ f)
    (hagrees : ∀ i ∈ U, i ∉ B → ∀ s, c i s = a i s)
    (hentry : ∀ i ∈ U, ∀ s, realContribution a i s ≤ δ * reference s)
    (hbudget : (f : ℝ) * δ ≤ ε) :
    IsCoreset (6 * ε) reference (cost (realContribution c) (matrixDecode c queries f U)) := by
  refine decode_correct (realContribution_nonneg ha) (realContribution_nonneg hc)
    hreference hε hεsmall hδ (α := 1) (by norm_num) hcoreset hB ?_ hentry ?_
    (fun Q i => rationalSensitivity c queries Q i) ?_ ?_
  · intro i hi hiB s
    simp only [realContribution, hagrees i hi hiB s]
  · simpa using hbudget
  · intro Q i _
    rw [rationalSensitivity_cast_eq hc hqueries]
    simp
  · intro Q i _
    rw [rationalSensitivity_cast_eq hc hqueries]

decl_257.name: FTC.Executable.stepCounted_deletions_le_one

decl_257.source:
theorem stepCounted_deletions_le_one (score : Finset I → I → ℚ) (Q : Finset I) :
    (stepCounted score Q).deletions ≤ 1 := by
  dsimp only [stepCounted]
  split <;> simp

decl_258.name: FTC.Executable.stepCounted_deletions_of_nonempty
decl_258.label: Executable.stepCounted_deletions_of_nonempty
decl_258.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Decoder.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_258.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder I] (score : Finset I → I → ℚ) {Q : Finset I},
  Q.Nonempty → (FTC.Executable.stepCounted score Q).deletions = 1
decl_258.source:
theorem stepCounted_deletions_of_nonempty (score : Finset I → I → ℚ)
    {Q : Finset I} (hQ : Q.Nonempty) : (stepCounted score Q).deletions = 1 := by
  have hn := selectedPair_ne_none (score Q) hQ
  cases hp : selectedPair (score Q) Q with
  | none => exact False.elim (hn hp)
  | some p =>
    have hp' : (maximumCounted (evaluateScores (score Q) (Q.sort (· ≤ ·))).1).1 =
        some p := hp
    simp only [stepCounted, hp']

decl_255.name: FTC.Executable.stepCounted_balance
decl_255.label: Executable.stepCounted_balance
decl_255.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Decoder.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_255.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder I] (score : Finset I → I → ℚ) (Q : Finset I),
  (FTC.Executable.stepCounted score Q).remaining.card + (FTC.Executable.stepCounted score Q).deletions = Q.card
decl_255.source:
theorem stepCounted_balance (score : Finset I → I → ℚ) (Q : Finset I) :
    (stepCounted score Q).remaining.card + (stepCounted score Q).deletions = Q.card := by
  by_cases hQ : Q.Nonempty
  · have hcard := card_selectionStep_add_one (rationalRule score) hQ
    rw [← stepCounted_remaining] at hcard
    simpa [stepCounted_deletions_of_nonempty score hQ] using hcard
  · have hz : Q = ∅ := Finset.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty.mp hQ
    subst Q
    simp [stepCounted, evaluateScores, maximumCounted]

decl_245.name: FTC.Executable.runCounted_balance
decl_245.label: Executable.runCounted_balance
decl_245.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Decoder.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_245.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder I] (score : Finset I → I → ℚ) (f : ℕ) (U : Finset I),
  (FTC.Executable.runCounted score f U).remaining.card + (FTC.Executable.runCounted score f U).deletions = U.card
decl_245.source:
theorem runCounted_balance (score : Finset I → I → ℚ) (f : ℕ) (U : Finset I) :
    (runCounted score f U).remaining.card + (runCounted score f U).deletions = U.card := by
  induction f generalizing U with
  | zero => simp [runCounted]
  | succ f ih =>
    by_cases hU : U.Nonempty
    · have hrest := ih (stepCounted score U).remaining
      have hfirst := stepCounted_balance score U
      simp only [runCounted, if_pos hU]
      omega
    · simp [runCounted, hU]

decl_247.name: FTC.Executable.runCounted_deletions_le
decl_247.label: Executable.runCounted_deletions_le
decl_247.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Decoder.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_247.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder I] (score : Finset I → I → ℚ) (f : ℕ) (U : Finset I),
  (FTC.Executable.runCounted score f U).deletions ≤ min f U.card
decl_247.source:
theorem runCounted_deletions_le (score : Finset I → I → ℚ) (f : ℕ) (U : Finset I) :
    (runCounted score f U).deletions ≤ min f U.card := by
  have hsteps : (runCounted score f U).deletions ≤ f := by
    induction f generalizing U with
    | zero => simp [runCounted]
    | succ f ih =>
      by_cases hU : U.Nonempty
      · have hrest := ih (stepCounted score U).remaining
        have hfirst := stepCounted_deletions_le_one score U
        simp only [runCounted, if_pos hU]
        omega
      · simp [runCounted, hU]
  have hbalance := runCounted_balance score f U
  omega

/-- Each actual sensitivity call on an intermediate subset has this unit-cost
arithmetic upper bound, by the backend's instrumented implementation. -/

decl_200.name: FTC.Executable.matrixOracle_work_le
decl_200.label: Executable.matrixOracle_work_le
decl_200.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Decoder.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_200.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : LinearOrder I] [DecidableEq S] (c : I → S → ℚ) (queries : Finset S)
  {Q U : Finset I},
  Q ⊆ U → ∀ (i : I), (FTC.Executable.rationalSensitivityCounted c queries Q i).2 ≤ queries.card * (2 * U.card + 3)
decl_200.source:
theorem matrixOracle_work_le (c : I → S → ℚ) (queries : Finset S)
    {Q U : Finset I} (hQU : Q ⊆ U) (i : I) :
    (rationalSensitivityCounted c queries Q i).2 ≤ queries.card * (2 * U.card + 3) := by
  rw [rationalSensitivityCounted_work]
  split_ifs
  · exact Nat.mul_le_mul_left _ (by have := Finset.card_le_card hQU; omega)
  · exact Nat.zero_le _

/-- Worst-case charge for the actual number of backend calls and cached-score
comparisons made by the counted loop. Every intermediate state is a subset of
`U`, so `matrixOracle_work_le` applies to every call. -/

decl_165.name: FTC.Executable.chargedMatrixWork
decl_165.label: Executable.chargedMatrixWork
decl_165.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Decoder.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_165.statement: {I : Type u_1} → {S : Type u_2} → [LinearOrder I] → (I → S → ℚ) → Finset S → ℕ → Finset I → ℕ

decl_166.name: FTC.Executable.chargedMatrixWork_bound
decl_166.label: Executable.chargedMatrixWork_bound
decl_166.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Decoder.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_166.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} {S : Type u_2} [inst : LinearOrder I] [DecidableEq S] (c : I → S → ℚ) (queries : Finset S) (f : ℕ)
  (U : Finset I),
  FTC.Executable.chargedMatrixWork c queries f U ≤ f * (U.card * queries.card * (2 * U.card + 3) + (U.card - 1))
decl_166.source:
theorem chargedMatrixWork_bound (c : I → S → ℚ) (queries : Finset S)
    (f : ℕ) (U : Finset I) :
    chargedMatrixWork c queries f U ≤
      f * (U.card * queries.card * (2 * U.card + 3) + (U.card - 1)) := by
  have hcalls := runCounted_scoreCalls_le (fun Q i => rationalSensitivity c queries Q i) f U
  have hcomparisons := runCounted_comparisons_le (fun Q i => rationalSensitivity c queries Q i) f U
  have hscaled := Nat.mul_le_mul_right (queries.card * (2 * U.card + 3)) hcalls
  unfold chargedMatrixWork matrixDecodeCounted
  calc
    _ ≤ (f * U.card) * (queries.card * (2 * U.card + 3)) + f * (U.card - 1) :=
      Nat.add_le_add hscaled hcomparisons
    _ = _ := by ring

end FTC.Executable

decl_177.name: FTC.Executable.evaluateScores
decl_177.label: Executable.evaluateScores

decl_177.source:
def evaluateScores (score : I → ℚ) : List I → List (I × ℚ) × ℕ
  | [] => ([], 0)
  | i :: is =>
      let tail := evaluateScores score is
      ((i, score i) :: tail.1, tail.2 + 1)

@[simp] theorem evaluateScores_values (score : I → ℚ) (is : List I) :
    (evaluateScores score is).1 = is.map (fun i => (i, score i)) := by

@[simp] theorem evaluateScores_calls (score : I → ℚ) (is : List I) :

  induction is with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons i is ih => simp [evaluateScores, ih]

/-- A maximum scan on cached values, charging exactly one comparison whenever
the nonempty tail already has a candidate. Ties retain the first candidate. -/

decl_202.name: FTC.Executable.maximumCounted
decl_202.label: Executable.maximumCounted
decl_202.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Filtering.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_202.statement: {I : Type u_1} → List (I × ℚ) → Option (I × ℚ) × ℕ
decl_202.source:
def maximumCounted : List (I × ℚ) → Option (I × ℚ) × ℕ
  | [] => (none, 0)
  | x :: xs =>
      let tail := maximumCounted xs
      match tail.1 with
      | none => (some x, tail.2)
      | some y => (some (if x.2 < y.2 then y else x), tail.2 + 1)

decl_204.name: FTC.Executable.maximumCounted_value
decl_204.label: Executable.maximumCounted_value
decl_204.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Filtering.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_204.statement: ∀ {I : Type u_1} (xs : List (I × ℚ)), (FTC.Executable.maximumCounted xs).1 = List.argmax Prod.snd xs
decl_204.source:
@[simp] theorem maximumCounted_value (xs : List (I × ℚ)) :
    (maximumCounted xs).1 = xs.argmax Prod.snd := by
  induction xs with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    rw [List.argmax_cons]
    simp only [maximumCounted]
    rw [← ih]
    cases h : (maximumCounted xs).1 with
    | none => simp [h]
    | some y =>
      by_cases hxy : x.2 < y.2 <;> simp [h, hxy]

decl_203.name: FTC.Executable.maximumCounted_comparisons
decl_203.label: Executable.maximumCounted_comparisons
decl_203.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Filtering.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_203.statement: ∀ {I : Type u_1} (xs : List (I × ℚ)), (FTC.Executable.maximumCounted xs).2 = xs.length - 1
decl_203.source:
@[simp] theorem maximumCounted_comparisons (xs : List (I × ℚ)) :
    (maximumCounted xs).2 = xs.length - 1 := by
  induction xs with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons x xs ih =>
    cases h : (maximumCounted xs).1 with
    | none =>
      have harg : xs.argmax (Prod.snd : I × ℚ → ℚ) = none := by
        rw [← maximumCounted_value]
        exact h
      have hnil : xs = [] := List.argmax_eq_none.mp harg
      subst xs
      rfl
    | some y =>
      have hne : xs ≠ [] := by intro hz; simp [hz, maximumCounted] at h
      have hlen : 0 < xs.length := by
        cases xs with
        | nil => exact False.elim (hne rfl)
        | cons a as => simp
      simp only [maximumCounted, h, List.length_cons]
      simp only [ih]
      omega

section OrderedIndices

variable [LinearOrder I]

/-- The cached maximum on a deterministic enumeration of a finite active set. -/

decl_250.name: FTC.Executable.selectedPair
decl_250.label: Executable.selectedPair
decl_250.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Filtering.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_250.statement: {I : Type u_1} → [LinearOrder I] → (I → ℚ) → Finset I → Option (I × ℚ)
decl_250.source:
def selectedPair (score : I → ℚ) (Q : Finset I) : Option (I × ℚ) :=
  (maximumCounted (evaluateScores score (Q.sort (· ≤ ·))).1).1

decl_251.name: FTC.Executable.selectedPair_eq_argmax
decl_251.label: Executable.selectedPair_eq_argmax
decl_251.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Filtering.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_251.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder I] (score : I → ℚ) (Q : Finset I),
  FTC.Executable.selectedPair score Q =
    List.argmax Prod.snd (List.map (fun i => (i, score i)) (Q.sort fun x1 x2 => x1 ≤ x2))
decl_251.source:
theorem selectedPair_eq_argmax (score : I → ℚ) (Q : Finset I) :
    selectedPair score Q =
      ((Q.sort (· ≤ ·)).map (fun i => (i, score i))).argmax Prod.snd := by
  simp [selectedPair]

decl_252.name: FTC.Executable.selectedPair_ne_none
decl_252.label: Executable.selectedPair_ne_none
decl_252.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Filtering.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_252.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder I] (score : I → ℚ) {Q : Finset I},
  Q.Nonempty → FTC.Executable.selectedPair score Q ≠ none
decl_252.source:
theorem selectedPair_ne_none (score : I → ℚ) {Q : Finset I} (hQ : Q.Nonempty) :
    selectedPair score Q ≠ none := by
  intro h
  rw [selectedPair_eq_argmax] at h
  have hnil := List.argmax_eq_none.mp h
  have hlen := congrArg List.length hnil
  simp only [List.length_map, Finset.length_sort, List.length_nil] at hlen
  exact (Finset.card_pos.mpr hQ).ne' hlen

/-- The fallback is unreachable for a nonempty set, but makes the algorithm
total without classical extraction from an existence statement. -/

decl_209.name: FTC.Executable.rationalChoice
decl_209.label: Executable.rationalChoice
decl_209.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Filtering.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_209.statement: {I : Type u_1} → [LinearOrder I] → (I → ℚ) → (Q : Finset I) → Q.Nonempty → I
decl_209.source:
def rationalChoice (score : I → ℚ) (Q : Finset I) (hQ : Q.Nonempty) : I :=
  match selectedPair score Q with
  | none => Q.min' hQ
  | some p => p.1

decl_210.name: FTC.Executable.rationalChoice_spec
decl_210.label: Executable.rationalChoice_spec
decl_210.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Filtering.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_210.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder I] (score : I → ℚ) (Q : Finset I) (hQ : Q.Nonempty),
  FTC.Executable.rationalChoice score Q hQ ∈ Q ∧ ∀ i ∈ Q, score i ≤ score (FTC.Executable.rationalChoice score Q hQ)
decl_210.source:
theorem rationalChoice_spec (score : I → ℚ) (Q : Finset I) (hQ : Q.Nonempty) :
    rationalChoice score Q hQ ∈ Q ∧
      ∀ i ∈ Q, score i ≤ score (rationalChoice score Q hQ) := by
  cases hp : selectedPair score Q with
  | none => exact False.elim (selectedPair_ne_none score hQ hp)
  | some p =>
    have hp' : p ∈ ((Q.sort (· ≤ ·)).map (fun i => (i, score i))).argmax Prod.snd := by
      rw [← selectedPair_eq_argmax, hp]
      simp
    have hmem := List.argmax_mem hp'
    obtain ⟨j, hj, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hmem
    constructor
    · simpa [rationalChoice, hp] using (Finset.mem_sort (· ≤ ·)).mp hj
    · intro i hi
      have hpair : (i, score i) ∈ (Q.sort (· ≤ ·)).map (fun i => (i, score i)) := by
        exact List.mem_map.mpr ⟨i, (Finset.mem_sort (· ≤ ·)).mpr hi, rfl⟩
      have hle := List.le_of_mem_argmax hpair hp'
      simpa [rationalChoice, hp] using hle

decl_234.name: FTC.Executable.rationalRule
decl_234.label: Executable.rationalRule

decl_234.source:
def rationalRule (score : Finset I → I → ℚ) : SelectionRule I where
  select Q h := rationalChoice (score Q) Q h

decl_235.name: FTC.Executable.rationalRule_isMaxFor
decl_235.label: Executable.rationalRule_isMaxFor
decl_235.summary: Declaration in FaultTolerantCoresets/Executable/Filtering.lean. See the Lean statement and proof below.
decl_235.statement:
∀ {I : Type u_1} [inst : LinearOrder I] (score : Finset I → I → ℚ),
  (FTC.Executable.rationalRule score).IsMaxFor fun Q i => ↑(score Q i)
decl_235.source:
theorem rationalRule_isMaxFor (score : Finset I → I → ℚ) :
    (rationalRule score).IsMaxFor (fun Q i => (score Q i : ℝ)) := by
  intro Q h i hi
  change (score Q i : ℝ) ≤ (score Q (rationalChoice (score Q) Q h) : ℝ)
  exact_mod_cast (rationalChoice_spec (score Q) Q h).2 i hi
